films.title: 3 Weeks After
films.synopsis: Three weeks after losing his best friend to suicide, Tzotza joins his classmates on a school excursion to Bulgaria despite still struggling with his grief. From the outset, it is clear he is an outsider. His classmates barely tolerate him, while his two teachers quietly do their best to protect him from their hostility. During a break at a highway rest area, Milica sneaks her boyfriend, Bogdanovic, onto the bus. It quickly becomes clear that he is the group's alpha—a charismatic troublemaker whose presence immediately shifts the dynamic. When the bus breaks down, the students and teachers are forced to take shelter in a nearly deserted resort preparing to close for the season. Cut off from the outside world, boredom and simmering tensions soon turn into cruelty, with Tzotza becoming the group's primary target. As the harassment escalates, a volatile confrontation forces long-buried resentments into the open, exposing an unsettling truth. The bullying reaches a devastating intensity, pushing Tzotza to his breaking point. Be warned: this is not a pleasant film. Depending on your state of mind, it may leave you emotionally devastated. Yet it is an essential work—a haunting portrait of a bored generation trapped in cruelty and apathy. It explores the perpetuation of bullying with unflinching honesty, revealing how easily victims and bystanders become part of its vicious circle. With 3 WEEKS AFTER, Serbian director Miroslav Terzić has crafted a powerful film that will shake you to the core. From its stunning cinematography, which beautifully underscores the characters' loneliness and isolation, to its meticulous sound design and immersive sound mix, every element works in harmony to create an unforgettable experience. It is probably the darkest film in this year's programme, but also—at least in my opinion—the most important. (ANNICK MAHNERT)

films.title: 5 More Minutes
films.synopsis: Close your eyes. Imagine the worst possible moment for you to be stuck in a time loop. For Antonio and Barbara, a last-ditch, no-reception weekend away meant to save their marriage is a strong contender. Do they even like each other anymore? Communication is broken, therapy talk is in bloom, a car nearly runs them over, a noisy plane flies overhead—and their couple’s weekend hasn’t even started. When they get to the house, Carlos, the guy from the agency, shows them around the property before they find themselves five minutes in the past. Over and over again. But the lesson they planned to teach their son the following Monday—that actions have consequences—will turn back on them. This is not your traditional time loop. Worldwide chaos, small-scale hell, the apocalypse on a domestic level. This unpredictable weekend quickly goes from bad to worse, but it might just be their marriage’s saving grace. This dark comedy flirts with thriller and horror elements in a very entertaining mix, and we can’t help but relish the escalating carnage as it bleeds far beyond the couple and Carlos. Built on the ongoing creative partnership between director Javier Ruiz Caldera and actor Berto Romero, the film is as sharply written as it is directed, claustrophobic in the best possible way. Romero, Belén Cuesta, and Javier Cámara show us how absurd and petty and downright cruel anyone can get. If five minutes are too short to fix anything, they are definitely long enough to make everything worse. (SONIA DROULHIOLE)

films.title: Adult Supervision
films.synopsis: Bill, a middle-aged father struggling to connect with his teenage daughter, volunteers to chaperone her school trip to the remote Klippvik archipelago, hoping a few days together might bridge the growing distance between them. Joined by fellow parents Pontus and Bobo, the three adults quickly become overwhelmed by the brutal social dynamics simmering through this group of children. ADULT SUPERVISION exposes the toxic "mean girls" culture that continues to thrive in schools, amplified by the relentless pressures of social media. While Pontus and Bobo dismiss the teenagers' behavior with jokes and misplaced observations, Bill is forced to relive painful memories of his own adolescence as the bullying escalates. What begins as an awkward school excursion gradually transforms into every parent's worst nightmare—a cautionary tale about unchecked cruelty, misguided authority, and adults whose good intentions prove tragically inadequate. In other words, it will have everyone questioning how anyone still has children or, if it's too late, whether they have a monster in the making back home. Balancing razor-sharp dark comedy with slow-burning psychological dread, the film builds its tension through mounting unease, escalating violence, and the unsettling realization of just how cruel ordinary people can become. The beautiful Swedish landscape provides a striking contrast to the increasingly disturbing events unfolding against its idyllic backdrop, showing that even those who appear trustworthy can reveal darker sides. Filled with morbid and sardonic humor, ADULT SUPERVISION contains moments that can be difficult to watch (those sensitive to animal cruelty, be warned—I wasn’t), delivering a disquieting portrait of adolescence and parenthood. (SARA LOPO)

films.title: A Prayer for the Dying
films.synopsis: Jacob, a Danish immigrant still haunted by his experiences in the Civil War, has built a new life in the town of Friendship. Serving as both priest and sheriff, he is called to retrieve a body found just beyond the town limits and escorts a disoriented woman, discovered wandering in a nearby field, back to the local doctor. After examining the corpse, the doctor warns Jacob that the man may have been carrying diphtheria. The woman may also be infected. When her husband arrives to take her home, the doctor attempts to warn him about the risk of contagion, but the man refuses to listen. Fearing an outbreak, the doctor urges Jacob to keep the diagnosis secret to prevent the townsfolk from panicking and trying to leave town. After Jacob suffers a personal loss, the doctor orders a quarantine just as a devastating bushfire changes course toward the town. Determined to protect the people in his care, Jacob is pushed to his breaking point. Trapped between a deadly epidemic and the approaching inferno, and having lost nearly everything he holds dear, Jacob struggles to preserve both the town and his own sanity. Based on Stewart O’Nan’s novel of the same name, Dara Van Dusen’s debut feature is nothing short of a gem—one that deserves to be experienced on the big screen. The film's assured direction, outstanding performances, and breathtaking cinematography immerse viewers in an apocalyptic story where the true threat isn't zombies or monsters, but the devastating consequences of human fear, ignorance, and poor decisions. It is a vision of hell on earth, set in a time when a single mistake could prove fatal and there was no turning back. (ANNICK MAHNERT)

films.title: Attack on Paradise
films.synopsis: Poor Suleyman. A comb taken for a weapon, his mother’s pills taken for drugs, one panicked attempt to fight back, one dead cop, and a seven-year jail sentence. Now, fresh out of prison, he only wants one thing: to reunite with his mother and atone for his absence. But as a friend warns him: “This is no longer Paradise, it’s hell.” Prince Hamza has taken over the Paradise apartment complex, surrounding himself with lackeys, enforcers, and killers, each floor with its own particular flavor of danger. Suleyman barely has time to see his mother before everything explodes: she needs her medicine, the police storm the building in a long-planned raid, and Hamza turns her into leverage. Forced into sharing the same objective as Yasmine, a rookie policewoman everyone underestimates, Suleyman has to fight his way up Paradise floor by floor. At this point, everyone wants him dead, and every new level brings a new threat, a new visual idea, and a new terrible choice. Close-quarters action? Check. Class rage and siege-movie tension? Check. Feverish visual flourishes? Absolutely. Bob Colaers’ ATTACK ON PARADISE turns a Belgian tower block into a full-contact descent into hell. Bones crunch, blood pools—this is visceral action at its finest. It is all anchored by co-writer and star Saïd Boumazoughe, whose sincere, guilt-ridden reluctance to engage slowly turns into a reckoning. Suleyman really chose the wrong day to come home. (SONIA DROULHIOLE)

films.title: Blood Feast
films.synopsis: There will never be another movie like BLOOD FEAST—the first "splatter" film in horror history. Written by Allison Louise Downe, produced by David F. Friedman, and directed by Herschell Gordon Lewis, BLOOD FEAST follows a caterer named Fuad Ramses who is hired to provide "an authentic Egyptian feast" for a birthday party. He wastes no time in committing unbelievable mutilation murders to appease an Egyptian goddess named Ishtar. John Waters said it best: "I first saw BLOOD FEAST at my local drive-in. When I saw teenage couples hopping from their cars to vomit, I knew I had found a movie after my own heart." A direct influence on Waters (MULTIPLE MANIACS), Frank Henenlotter (BASKET CASE), and dozens of 1980s slashers, BLOOD FEAST erupts with pop-art brain-bludgeons, tabloid-style ghoulishness, and pitch-black gallows humor. The movie's legendary status as a subversive benchmark is enhanced by the contributions of Allison Louise Downe—a writer, producer, special effects artist, actor, and assistant director who deserves to be immortalized for her contributions to horror and exploitation history. AGFA and Something Weird are honored to unleash the definitive presentation of this seminal splatterfest—newly restored in 4K from the original camera negative for the first time ever. (AGFA)

films.title: Bloody Tennis
films.synopsis: Tennis has somehow become the coolest sport among all my friends in France. Sophie has a rather different experience. Sent to a summer academy in Southern Europe to hone her skills—skills the director is not convinced she even possesses—she enters a SUSPIRIA-inspired world where something feels wrong from the start. Every morning, the students must swallow a strange-smelling, gooey, chunky, blood-red smoothie. Cats are disappearing. Her roommate keeps her medication hidden inside a teddy bear. And as Sophie forms relationships with the women around her through friendship, rivalry, and desire, we come to understand that this will be a very bloody, very strange, sporting coming-of-age story. The deeper Sophie gets, the more extreme the academy’s methods become. Leeches are used to improve performance, and a deeply unsettling assistant may know something about those missing cats. He is certainly the reason I found myself googling, “What is catgut actually made of?” I will let you discover the answer to that one on your own. But the strangeness never sidelines the sport: Sophie begins proving the director wrong, and the more she succeeds, the more power the academy gains over her. Nikias Chryssos pushes familiar ideas about discipline, sacrifice, and competitive excellence into grotesque territory, turning the academy into a satire of performance culture itself: a world where every body must be optimized, every weakness corrected, and almost any damage can be reframed as commitment if it produces a winner. Hello, modern world. But the satire lands because Sophie genuinely wants what the academy is offering. The better she becomes, the more willing she is to accept its logic, and the price is paid through the people around her. With its sun-washed whites, eruptions of blood-red, and queasy humor, BLOODY TENNIS is as visually playful as it is unexpectedly emotional.

films.title: BURNT ENDominations
films.synopsis: In 2025, we just happened to assemble some animated shorts in the right combination and opened up a portal to another world. A place where cats had wings, demonic miniatures could wield the power of a universe in a single blow, and girls could be girls. We inadvertently created a rift in the frontal cortex of someone's medulla oblongata, and we had to take a blood oath to never speak of it again. Well… we broke that oath, and in exchange, had to sacrifice three programmers to the fiery pits of hell; two of them were made of clay, so it didn't turn out to be a huge loss. Now that we have danced with the devil, we return to tell more tales, melt more minds, and feast on the fears of unknowing. BURNT ENDominations is back, and ballsier than ever!!! We brought in guest curators Ashley Sengstaken, Robbie Ward, and Skinner to deliver you directly to a midnight mass from the forbidden side of the cartoon dial. Tune in. Trip out. And keep your hands and legs inside the vehicle at all times. *Please note that the films are listed in alphabetical order, not in screening order. DEMONI FEROX: NIGHT PEOPLE STOLE MY BABY USA, 2023 North American Premiere, 5 min Director - Thomas J Yagodinski Surreal nightmares haunt a young couple until late one stormy night, when they are visited by the Night People. I HAVE A UK, 2026 Texas Premiere, 5 min Director - Rory Waudby-Tolley A man lists the things he has. MOTHER EARTH USA, 2026 World Premiere, 17 min Director - Jimmy ScreamerClauz An alien race weaponizes humanity’s anger and fear, turning the people of Earth against one another until mankind destroys itself. But as the last humans fall, the invaders discover something their species has never known and cannot manufacture. A mother’s love. SHOWGIRLS - THE DA DA EDIT USA, 2026 Texas Premiere, 2 min Director - Julia Chien A lesbian rewrite of an already lesbian film.

films.title: Carrie (two episodes)
films.synopsis: Misfit high‑schooler Carrie White (Summer H. Howell) has spent her life hidden away inside the walls of her home with her fiercely protective mother, Margaret (Samantha Sloyan). After her father’s sudden, untimely death thrusts her into the unforgiving ecosystem of public high school, Carrie is forced to navigate a viral bullying scandal that tears through her community, the relentless pressure and casual cruelty of the social‑media age, and the awakening of mysterious telekinetic powers that rise alongside her adolescence. Told over eight propulsive episodes, the series expands King’s cultural landmark — deepening its characters and tensions, and following the small, everyday choices that build toward a single, shattering night, in a gripping, deeply human story about kindness versus cruelty, and whether we’re witnessing the making of a hero, a monster, or something far more complicated. (AMAZON MGM STUDIOS)

films.title: Cinema Recomposed: Silent Monsters
films.synopsis: A live string quartet plays new scores for seven classic silent horror short films. Seven composers, aged 17 to 24, composed new scores for silent short films under the mentorship of some of the industry's top professionals. This is CINEMA RECOMPOSED! Commissioned by Golden Hornet, in partnership with a team including Tim League (Alamo Drafthouse Cinema, Metro Cinema) and the American Genre Film Archive (AGFA), this is the second year that Fantastic Fest will host a screening with a live score performed by the Invoke string quartet. The next generation of film composers is here! This year’s short films include the following: THE THIEVING HAND (1908) FRANKENSTEIN (1910) DR. JEKYLL AND MR. HYDE (1912) THE GHOST OF SLUMBER MOUNTAIN (1919) HÄXAN: HELL SEQUENCE (1922) HELL'S BELLS (1929) THE HAUNTED SHIP (1930) Golden Hornet partnered with fellow 501(c)(3) non-profit, the American Genre Film Archive (AGFA), to bring the second edition of CINEMA RECOMPOSED to life. AGFA is the world’s largest archive dedicated to genre movies and filmmakers. We provide each composer with something that's often not accessible through traditional music programs: one-on-one access to composers working at the highest level. With help from Tim League and our Artistic Director, Graham Reynolds, we have assembled a team of some of Hollywood's best film composers to mentor each young artist, including Mark Orton, David Wingo, Brian Reitzell, Nicoletta Nomicou, and more! (GOLDEN HORNET)

films.title: Compliance
films.synopsis: As a company relations rep for the tech startup and homestay hotel brand UVisit, Sam closes all of the indemnifying loops when something goes wrong... a job she performs with increasing exhaustion and disillusionment. She has uprooted her life to LA to kick heartbreak and a drinking habit, only to find herself investigating a sexual assault case that could land her employer in hot water and further dissolve her conscience. Some of you may be reading this from a beautifully printed guide, pages earmarked with your most anticipated titles of this year’s festival. I’m willing to bet more of you are reading this scrolling on your phone, toggling between this movie and other equally wonderful options in your screening block. I bet that, for an extra few bucks to our vendor, we could track each swipe or click and then use that data to inform some sort of nefarious decision. That’s because, of course, surveillance and conspiracy are central tenets of contemporary digital life—all of the data captured by all of the various entities and agencies feels illusory until it falls under their control, or becomes an issue of liability. This is as good a space as any to note that COMPLIANCE deals with brutal and thorny issues of consent and complicity, fueled by the shifting visual perspectives that modern screen life offers—computer screens, wearables, and cameras hidden from view. Such a complex visual and emotional schema gives way to a dark web (and Dark Web!) of power, corruption, and lies. COMPLIANCE is the feel-bad movie of the fest, or at least, one of twelve. Don’t say we didn’t warn you! (JAKE ISGAR)

films.title: Corpus
tags: Girls Just Want to Have Fun
films.synopsis: The quietly horrifying cold open of CORPUS is quickly replaced by a REAL WORLD-esque title sequence and the grimy, pulsing late 1990s club scene in NYC. Sayo, equal parts photographer and coke dealer, and his friends, trust fund baby Ross and the scene’s hottest new model Vince, enjoy a sweaty, sexually-charged night clubbing and reconnecting in Sayo’s dark room, before heading out to an exclusive, secluded modelling industry party at Vince’s insistence. From the blood-soaked opening moments at the remote estate, it’s clear nothing this weekend will be as advertised. The promised industry professionals turn out to be one well-known photographer, Billie, and her sapphic housemates, the elderly Cata and amateur poultry farmer Wren. The awkward introductions quickly become a series of sensual dinners, absinthe-fueled debauchery, midnight skinny dipping, and philosophical conversations around a bonfire. Balancing escalating sexual tension with a pervasive sense of unease, Corrin Evans makes her feature film directorial debut with a script co-written with Lily Cowles, delivering subdued tension and nuanced queer characters. Paired with beautiful visuals that are equally gory and erotic, CORPUS culminates in a frenetic and surprising third act that scratches an itch you didn’t know you had and lingers in the back of your mind long after the final credits roll. (KEV DOOLEY)

films.title: Death Has No Master
films.synopsis: After the death of her father, Caro travels from Italy to Venezuela to sell her childhood home, an aging estate with a cacao plantation. Upon arriving at the mansion, she discovers it is occupied by Sonia, a former employee, and her young son, Maiko. Sympathetic to their situation, Caro initially agrees to share the house, moving into her parents' old bedroom while Sonia remains in the main living quarters. She also finds out that Sonia has been illegally subletting rooms to other tenants. When Caro explains that she intends to sell the property and tries to politely ask everyone to leave, Sonia refuses, insisting she has just as much right to remain there as Caro does. Seeking help, Caro tries to file a complaint at the local police station against the squatters, only to be warned against escalating the conflict. In the close-knit community, Sonia and her son are well known, and the authorities have little interest in intervening. As the standoff intensifies, Caro exhausts her options and turns to her father's former lawyer, hoping he can resolve the situation. But what begins as an attempt to intimidate the occupants quickly spirals into violence, drawing Caro into the country's deep-rooted legacy of dispossession and brutality—one that refuses to remain buried. In Jorge Thielen Armand’s pressure-cooker thriller, Asia Argento plays an expat who returns to the country she fled as a child following her father’s death, only to find herself at odds with the locals, their customs, and their way of life. A classic fish out of water, Caro has little regard for those around her, her sole concern being the money she stands to make from selling the family estate. She becomes the embodiment of colonialism, capitalism, and entrenched social inequality.

films.title: Death of a Yellow Bird
films.synopsis: After deciding to halt cancer treatment, an unnamed man travels to his family’s old cabin in the dead of a snowy winter to find some peace and quiet. Alone, with no outside contact besides difficult, strained conversations with his mother and wife, he starts to sense a strange presence. Haunted by a tragedy he can’t quite remember, finding an old camcorder and a collection of VHS home videos only makes the strangeness feel more acute. In an attempt to find some stability in his isolation, the man begins to film videos for his young son, but distortions and threatening sounds on the recorded tapes convince the man there is a ghost with him. Cody Calahan’s film is a heartrending, beautiful examination of grief, family, and sacrifice. While the "cabin in the woods" horror movie is certainly a genre staple, Calahan’s deployment of stark imagery and an otherworldly soundscape give the audience a sense of emotional trauma more than creeping, violent dread. Long scenes of fresh snow and a dim cabin are punctuated by bright, sunlit flashbacks and home movies of the man’s childhood at the cabin with his family. When the man begins to hear the mysterious presence in his recordings, the film’s sound uses garbled, staticky words to communicate the otherworldliness of the entity and the man’s own mysterious past and identity. Would it surprise you to know the director was a producer on the soundscape horror UNDERTONE from earlier this year? If Terrence Malick made a ghost movie, it might look something like DEATH OF A YELLOW BIRD. Torn between memory and the future, the protagonist is stuck in an alienating environment with a need for emotional closure to resolve his responsibility for a lingering familial trauma. With a final act that crosses time, this slow-burn, atmospheric horror movie builds to an unexpected finale.

films.title: Dieux Par Dupieux: Full Phil & Vertiginous
films.synopsis: Enjoy a double feature from the unbelievably prolific Fantastic Fest favorite Quentin Dupieux! FULL PHIL: Deep in the bush, mad scientists Chad (Tim Heidecker) and Andy (Eric Wareheim) make the discovery of a lifetime—a head-chomping dime-store creature from the lagoon who may unlock the secret to eternal life. Naturally, they’re the leads of a ‘50s B-movie being enjoyed by a famished Madeleine Doom (Kristen Stewart), languishing in a posh Parisian hotel with her estranged father, Phil (Woody Harrelson). Phil is hoping that an all-expense trip to the City of Love will help him reconnect with his daughter, but their increasing discontent arouses the suspicion of the hotel’s head of hospitality (Charlotte Le Bon), who takes it upon herself to surveil them throughout the evening. Prolific prankster Quentin Dupieux is no stranger to Fantastic Fest audiences, and FULL PHIL will certainly not bring any new converts to the cause. This feature-length Aristocrats joke, with its disparate threads, monstah movie bona fides, and casual body horror, builds to a climax that’ll have your belly shakin’ with uneasy laughter. (JAKE ISGAR) VERTIGINIOUS: Ever wondered whether we all live in a simulation? The idea has fascinated many for decades, even before films such as THE MATRIX or philosopher Nick Bostrom propelled it into the mainstream. In VERTIGINOUS, Quentin Dupieux offers his own delightfully off-kilter take on the concept, brought to life through the voice of French actor Alain Chabat, whose character Jacky is desperate to prove to his friend Bruno (Jonathan Cohen) that they are living in a simulation. As anyone familiar with Dupieux's work might expect, this is neither a grand science-fiction dystopia nor a sleek technological utopia. Instead, it is a razor-sharp satire that turns the simulation hypothesis into an absurdly funny mirror of contemporary life.

films.title: Dog God
films.synopsis: Long regarded as one of the most elusive works in Thai cinema, DOGGOD emerges from almost 30 years of censorship as a gleefully anarchic act of cinematic heresy. Shot on 16mm with the help of friends and family on a shoestring budget, Ing K.'s cult underground piece blends black comedy, religious satire, and outsider independent filmmaking to question blind faith and blind following. When Victor Strong, a cult investigator, arrives in Bangkok to rescue a young woman from a New Age sect, he finds himself drawn into an increasingly bizarre world where devotees worship a stray dog as a divine being and charismatic gurus spin ever-more-elaborate spiritual ruses. Beginning with the tone of an absurd farce, the film gradually reveals itself as a razor-sharp critique of religious authority and collective delusion as our protagonist sinks deeper into this universe. Banned by Thai authorities in 1998 for allegedly insulting religion, DOGGOD, originally titled MY TEACHER EATS BISCUITS, became a legendary "lost" film, circulating only through rare international screenings. Newly restored and re-edited by the director, the film returns not as a historical curiosity but as a strikingly contemporary provocation. By turns outrageous, camp, and challenging, Ing K.'s singular vision stands as a landmark of Southeast Asian independent cinema and a defiant testament to the enduring power of artistic dissent. (SARA LOPO)

films.title: Donkey Princess
films.synopsis: After the death of her mother, Princess Diana is raised by her grieving father in the Kingdom of Chile. The king finds solace in crafting whimsical toys for his daughter while imposing a cruel decree: anyone who succumbs to the plague of love will be exiled to the Valley of Thorns. On her birthday, Diana encounters Lalo, a young huaso (Chilean cowboy) whose unexplainable arrival awakens forbidden feelings she has never experienced. Smitten by the princess, he gives her a magical bracelet capable of granting any wish, with the caveat that each wish transports its owner to another kingdom in another time, potentially harming those one loves. The couple’s affair is discovered and Lalo is banished to the Valley of Thorns; Diana, heartbroken, uses the bracelet's wish-granting capabilities to reunite with him, embarking on a journey across space and time. Taking Charles Perrault’s fairy tale “Donkeyskin” as a guiding star, DONKEY PRINCESS reimagines its themes of identity, abandonment, transformation, and the ways we reshape ourselves after trauma. Directors Cristóbal León and Joaquín Cociña continue expanding the visual language established in THE WOLF HOUSE and THE HYPERBOREANS, crafting a purely formalist live-action feature filled with magical handcrafted worlds and haunting beauty. Rooted in Chilean pop culture and folklore while paying homage to the dreamlike aesthetics of Jan Švankmajer and Yuri Norstein, the filmmakers transform the different worlds' fears of the plague into an exploration of grief and the fantasies we create to escape our losses. DONKEY PRINCESS understands that longing can be both a source of hope and a trap, and that sometimes we just miss something simply because we imagine how extraordinary it could be.

films.title: Drawn & Quartered
films.synopsis: Marvel at the diversity of human expression in our annual celebration of animation in all its varied forms and styles. From furry fables, to verite speculative fiction rendered with glass and soil, to monochrome meditations on would-be parenthood, and colorful, psychedelic alien romance, there’s no limit to the handmade pleasures to be found in this sampling of animated wonders from across the globe. *Please note: films listed in alphabetical order, not in order of appearance in the block. EIGHT UNCOMFORTABLE ROBOTS - Dir. James Reinebold Feel free to browse The Optimax Corporation’s new product catalog, showcasing an array of robots plagued by technical problems and existential afflictions. INSECTICIDE - Dir. Paula Gallego González When a grotesque insect succumbs to his kinky attraction to a strange TV screen, he bears witness to a lustful and chaotic world that leads to deadly consequences. Yes, you read that right. THE MAGICIAN - Dir. Joe Garber Unlock a new fear you didn't think you had in you: spider-like magicians that kidnap babies and make terrible life-partners. PENGUIN - Dir. Kaspar Jancis When a hunter returns from Antarctica with a stuffed penguin, an impulsive act of carnal desire leads to an unfortunate accident and an irreversible, bizarre shift in their relationship. PRE-PARENTING - Dir. Yu Yu In the near future, special glasses allow expectant parents to see what their child’s life might look like, but an accident turns this gift into a curse for Shu-Han. A delicately rendered stop-motion drama about learning to live with lost potentialities. SHAPE OF YOUR HEART - Dir. Leonid Shmelkov This hypnotically mind-warping tale of an Earth after alien intervention leaves us with few remnants to hold onto: the shape of our own hearts, and the ankles of towering, all-powerful dominatrix. films.title: Fantastic Shorts
films.synopsis: Welcome to our annual "something for everyone" block where, this year, you're invited to contemplate the myriad ways that nothing in this world is what it seems, and that the future is neither guaranteed nor fully predetermined. Join various lovelorn souls, disillusioned mortals, aspiring artists, and vengeful survivors as they jump head first into the mysteries of life and death. *Please note: films listed in alphabetical order, not in order of appearance in the block. DEAD ANGLE- Dir. Cristian Beteta When Ramón agrees to meet his ex-wife Estela to discuss the wrongful death of their teenaged son, he has no idea that a revenge plot has already been set in motion. What you don’t know will destroy you in this cold-blooded Goya-winning thriller. FESTER- Dir. Max Parr Unchecked jealousy will swell and fester in our guts until it transforms us from the inside. Canadian dark humo(u)r done right, replete with toilet-based teleportation. GOSSAMER- Dir. Federico Barni A singer undergoes an irrevocable metamorphosis after seeking the help of a biotech firm to restore her lost voice in this Cronenbergian sci-fi that merges with a live progressive metal performance. Featuring music by Rolo Tomassi. IS THIS DESIRE?- Dir. Apa Agbayani A derelict mansion unlocks a woman’s deepest yearning in this erotic riff on Henry James. A modern Filipino gothic replete with beautiful boys, green lasers, and passion fruit. JIMMY'S CUSTOM COFFIN- Dir. James P. Gannon Jimmy has cancer and some grand ideas for his funeral, all in keeping with his trickster personality. James (documentarian and FF alum) turns his camera towards capturing the spirit of his friend Jimmy, in his final months. RICHARD GOES ON A DATE- Dir. Johnny Frohman This tone-perfect awkward comedy shows why dating today is a total drag. It's bad enough when he doesn't like your pet, and even worse when he has telekinetic powers.

films.title: Flapjax
films.synopsis: Arrow Bentley is the most enthusiastic restaurant manager you have ever seen. He spends the night in a spare room off the kitchen, he works more shifts than he needs to, and he talks to the cartoon pig mascot who plasters every inch of the kitschy dining room. Does he work at the freshest, coolest fast food joint in New York? Nope! He works at Hamudders, a pork-based eatery with the nutritional value of a landfill and a taste that would have killed the SUPERSIZE ME guy in three days. Arrow’s enthusiasm and can-do attitude have finally been noticed, and the big guys over at Hamudders HQ have trusted Arrow to relaunch a long out-of-circulation product pulled for unknown reasons: Flapjax. He’s got a short time to plan the world premiere with his one-hit-wonder mom, his best employee trying to quit, and his growing suspicion that the Flapjax itself is hiding something sinister. Take a bit of LOONEY TUNES, a dash of Troma, add a hint of Brian Yuzna, and you have the recipe for Rocko Zevenbergen‘s FLAPJAX. This fast food horror-comedy delivers on all the fronts you’d want from such a concoction: movement amplified by silly noises, a musical number, and some gonzo practical effects. Each bit of Zevenbergen’s film is filled with sight gags, handmade production design, and satire. If you think an overzealous middle manager and his corporate bosses with nefarious interests have nothing to say about the modern American experience, then you haven’t been paying attention. Advertisements plaster over almost every inch of available space, and at all times one must consume, consume, consume… So consume this feast you must! FLAPJAX is sure to go into the darkest corners of your stomach and sure to be a blast with a Fantastic Fest audience. (AUSTIN KING) Paired with the short UDDERS! dir.

films.title: Fresh Frights with Rotten Tomatoes
films.synopsis: Join Rotten Tomatoes and Tomatometer-approved critics for a lively conversation about all things horror. Get obsession-worthy horror recommendations, insider tips for writing sharper reviews, and expert advice on finding gems on the ground at film festivals.

films.title: Fright or Wrong Trivia
films.synopsis: Join hosts Brad McHargue and Becky Sayers for an evening of horror trivia madness with unique themed rounds. Assemble your crew of horror nerds (up to 6 players per team) and compete for a chance to win killer prizes and most importantly, the bragging rights that come with knowing you're better than everyone else!

films.title: Frisk
films.synopsis: Dennis is a god. He’s got charm oozing out of his round pectorals, a square jaw without a wisp of facial hair, and a stare to make most anyone submit to his masculinity. Even his overwhelming desire to murder for sexual pleasure would make him the perfect poster boy for an All-American classic. There’s just one hiccup: Dennis is gay. His serial killer daydreams are concentrated on the young, attractive men he brings home, though he hasn’t actually killed anyone yet. He is quite open with his friends about his fantasies, but they think Dennis is just acting out an extreme roleplay fetish. It’s time for Dennis to leave the world of fantasy and pop his murder cherry. When FRISK premiered at the Frameline Film Festival in 1995, it seemed the queer audience wasn’t quite sure what to do with it. Tales circulate about a mass walkout from The Castro with exiting festival attendees yelling at the movie screen, and the film is still banned from distribution or showcase within the UK. Some people have labeled the film "controversial." Almost all of the main characters are unrepentant sociopaths, and the erotic fantasies are rendered with an uncritical eye toward violence, blood, and torture. With the attack on queer rights and people on the rise in the world, and certainly at the time of the film’s original premiere, it’s not hard to see why a film featuring some of the worst queer people alive would ruffle some feathers. Revisiting the film 31 years later, I found Todd Verow’s adaptation of the Dennis Cooper novel to be unapologetic, viscerally kinky, and undeniably erotic. A film exploring some of our most monstrous desires, with a fresh new hunk destined for the butcher’s block every ten minutes, is not for everyone. I loved it.

films.title: Future Tense
films.synopsis: In the near future, the world is suffering from the effects of climate change, provoking mass migration and civil unrest across the globe. With this backdrop, a young couple books a romantic time-travel experience, promising to take people back to a pristine world unmarred by the current ravages of overpopulation. When they land, they are greeted by a beautiful, lush landscape, luxury accommodations, and blissful silence. But the trip takes a sharp turn when one of them reveals their true intentions, resulting in a conflict that has higher stakes beyond just the personal. We are pleased to welcome Jenna Cato Bass back to Fantastic Fest, after having screened her psychological horror film GOOD MADAM in 2021. A subtle science fiction that grapples with timely issues like climate change and wealth inequality through a genre lens, Bass has crafted a film that’s equally entertaining and intelligent. The two leads have incredible chemistry, guiding us through a range of emotions and shifting allegiances throughout the film. FUTURE TENSE doesn’t offer any easy solutions, opting for a continually surprising and thought-provoking journey, in a dystopian future that seems a little too realistic for comfort. (LISA DREYER)

films.title: Game Master
films.synopsis: GAME MASTER marks renowned French comedian Éric Judor’s return to the director’s chair for the big screen with a joyous celebration of imagination, awkward parenthood, and the transformative power of play that ventures deep into the wonderfully eccentric world of live-action role-playing. Alexandre, played by Éric Judor himself, is an exasperated father desperate to put his daughter Isaure onto what he thinks is the right path. When he hears that she is skipping an important business-school interview, Alexandre infiltrates a sprawling medieval fantasy LARP to find his daughter in an irresistibly funny adventure. Judor, whose singular blend of deadpan absurdism and emotional sincerity has made his films enduring cult favorites, crafts a comedy that affectionately skewers fantasy fandom while embracing the generosity, creativity, and community that define it. Trading corporate frustrations for enchanted forests, foam swords, and elaborately improvised kingdoms, his reluctant hero discovers that the greatest challenge isn't slaying mythical beasts, but confronting the compromises and disappointments of adulthood, turning what begins as an embarrassing rescue mission into an unexpectedly heartfelt quest of self-discovery. GAME MASTER balances broad physical comedy with genuine emotional warmth, never losing sight of the father-daughter relationship at its core. The film's lovingly realized LARP setting becomes both playground and emotional battleground, where elves, orcs, scheming nobles, and enthusiastic hobbyists coexist in a delightfully convincing parallel reality. Bursting with infectious energy and a deep affection for outsiders who refuse to stop dreaming, the film is not just a fantasy spoof or family reconciliation story; it’s also an ode to unapologetic geek culture and a pleasant reminder that growing up doesn’t have to mean leaving the magic behind.

films.title: Ghost in the Cell
films.synopsis: Within the confines of an Indonesian prison where violent criminals, corrupt officials, and privileged white-collar offenders coexist under an oppressive regime, the arrival of a mysterious new inmate unleashes a terrifying force that turns this institution into the perfect setting for a feverish supernatural siege. Bodies start piling up and prisoners are transformed into grotesque works of art. In a place where violence is routine, these macabre acts shock even the toughest inmates. As panic spreads, rival gangs, outcasts, and prison authorities are forced into an uneasy alliance. They must uncover the origins of the malevolent entity before it consumes the institution from within, but they quickly realize that not everyone (and certainly not everything) can be bribed, controlled, or contained. Blending outrageous gore, explosive action, unexpected comedy, and biting social commentary, Indonesian genre visionary Joko Anwar delivers his most deliriously ambitious film yet: a blood-soaked fusion of supernatural horror, prison thriller, martial arts action, and pitch-black political satire. GHOST IN THE CELL uses its supernatural premise to expose the corruption, inequality, and moral decay festering beneath the surface of contemporary society, haunting one of Indonesia’s most notorious social institutions with its own sins. Wildly inventive and playfully excessive, the film confirms Joko Anwar as one of contemporary genre cinema's most audacious voices. (SARA LOPO)

films.title: Gimme Truth
films.synopsis: What happens when you lose all trust in corporate and governmental institutions? In the age of misinformation and citizen sleuths, it is not hard to understand how one could become so easily intertwined with conspiracy thinking after such disillusionment. From chemtrails and extraterrestrials to alternative archaeology and pandemic conspiracies, GIMME TRUTH ventures into the ever-expanding landscape of contemporary belief by exploring the human appeal and social consequences of such reasoning. Rather than ridicule or endorse their film's subjects, directors Brad Abrahams and Simon Ennis approach conspiracy culture with curiosity and empathy, following individuals whose search for hidden truths has become central to their identities. As their participants pursue enlightenment, certainty, and community beyond the boundaries of mainstream institutions, the film asks what happens when personal conviction begins to outweigh shared evidence, and when these beliefs become more than just theories. The documentary never tries to prove or debunk any of these theories, but rather tries to understand how they can become a source of purpose or a framework through which one tries to make sense of an increasingly fragmented world. By turns surprising, unsettling, darkly humorous, and unexpectedly compassionate, GIMME TRUTH offers a nuanced portrait of a society struggling to agree on what is real, serving as a deep analysis of what it means when the search for truth becomes a way of life. (SARA LOPO) *Paired with the short SUPER ABSOLUTELY dir. Francesca Pazniokas This is a dating video. It has nothing to do with our Reptilian Overlords. Why do you keep bringing up our Reptilian Overlords?

films.title: Girl in the Night
tags: Girls Just Want to Have Fun
films.synopsis: Rok is trapped in the fluorescent existential purgatory of his monotonous work at a gas station. His greatest act of rebellion is pocketing the occasional chocolate bar during his night shift. One evening, a bruised young woman stumbles into his store. By night, she's a self-appointed vigilante, roaming the city in search of missing pets, lost objects, and the kinds of crimes everyone else is too tired to notice. Desperate for a connection with this enigmatic lass, and burdened by his own terrible instincts, Rok steals her bicycle. As the “sole witness” of the crime, and with the promise of finding her lost bike, Rok joins her nightly capers. The pair navigate a nocturnal world populated by eccentrics and loners, with every interaction leading them deeper into a city where social detachment and boredom feel like the greatest danger haunting its residents. After shattering Slovenian box-office records with his debut feature, AT HOSTAR, Luka Marčetić returns with a delightfully deadpan love letter to misfits and the spirit of youth. Equal parts a melancholy hangout comedy and a lo-fi vigilante romp, GIRL IN THE NIGHT is packed with awkward encounters and quiet optimism. This absurdist crowd-pleaser reminds us that sometimes changing the world starts with helping someone find what they've lost, even if you're the reason it went missing in the first place. (RAFAEL RODRIGUEZ)
