films.title: Godmother
films.synopsis: Romantic desert oasis weekend trip tip #47: Nothing good will happen when your first vacation jam is Eric Carmen’s yacht rock standard "Make Me Lose Control." Colby, a formulaic debonair fintech-type dude, has meticulously planned the perfect couples' weekend at a Pueblo Revival-style home in the New Mexico high desert for his girlfriend, Theo. But all his strategizing gets put on the sideline once Theo invites her free-spirited sister Katie, fresh off a painful breakup. As if the clashing personalities between Colby and Katie weren't enough for Theo, the trio's rental home hosts, the seemingly gracious Martinsons, played by horror legends Dee Wallace and Bruce Davison, harbor unsettling motives for the fate of the couple. Trapped between Colby's safe and controlling predictability and Katie's reckless spontaneity, Theo finds herself mediating her loved ones' tensions while the isolated desert retreat is gestating something increasingly strange and devilish. Spending a few holidays with my family under the spell of Las Cruces’s Organ Mountains and the beautiful Mesilla Valley, I can understand why director John Veron chose this enchanting and mystical place as the setting for his debut film. Co-written with gaming personality Alanah Pearce and executive produced with the guidance of streaming superstar Seán McLoughlin (Jacksepticeye), GODMOTHER explores the compromises we make for love and identity. The film also presents a thoughtful contrast between older generations' couple expectations and more contemporary relationship goals. For Theo and the audience, in the words of the late Eric Carmen, this nightmarish desert retreat will "take you over the edge, make you lose control." (RAFAEL RODRIGUEZ)

films.title: Half
films.synopsis: Ivy and her twin brother are no ordinary siblings. Born half-human, half-vampire, they were raised by their mother to always look out for one another. Now adults, the twins set off on a road trip, only to be ambushed by a ruthless gang of scavengers who leave them for dead. As night falls, their bodies regenerate, revealing the full extent of their vampire heritage. With a newfound thirst for vengeance, the twins embark on a bloody mission to hunt down every last one of their attackers. HALF is an exhilarating blend of action, thriller, and horror, packed with genuinely memorable set pieces. Give it a moment, and once it hits full throttle, it never lets up. Brutal, gory, and consistently funny, this Malayalam vampire film marks Samjad's second feature. The action sequences, choreographed by Very Tri Yulisman—best known for THE RAID 2 and THE NIGHT COMES FOR US—are a major highlight. Most importantly, HALF never takes itself too seriously, and that's exactly why it works. It's a film determined to entertain, and Samjad knows precisely how to deliver a wildly enjoyable ride. (ANNICK MAHNERT)

films.title: Hell House
films.synopsis: This church wants to scare the hell out of you. Literally. HELL HOUSE is a fly-on-the-wall documentary that follows the Trinity Assembly of God Church in Dallas, Texas, as they build a "hell house" for the Y2K Halloween season. Hell houses are the evangelical Christian church’s answer to a haunted house—a Fundamentalist fright night meant to scare the bejesus out of any nonbeliever. But instead of Draculas and Freddy Kruegers, the church recreates scenes that graphically depict modern-day "evils" such as botched abortions, AIDS-related deaths, fatal drunk driving crashes, date rapes, and drug-induced suicides. Shot on gorgeous 16mm film stock by director George Ratliff and friends, HELL HOUSE is an outrageous, enthralling, and poignant vérité window into the creative effort and religious zeal behind this over-the-top event. The film chronicles the entire hell house process, from the initial script meeting to the lavish production design, while also remaining an intimate portrait of the people who fervently believe its message. Fans of AMERICAN MOVIE, EXIT THROUGH THE GIFT SHOP, and MISTER ORGAN take note: this movie might be your new favorite obsession. AGFA is honored to present a new restoration of HELL HOUSE from the original 16mm camera negative for the first time ever with director George Ratliff in person. (AGFA)

films.title: Henry: Portrait of a Serial Killer
films.synopsis: Brand-new 40th anniversary 35mm print! One of the most harrowing films of the 20th century, HENRY: PORTRAIT OF A SERIAL KILLER is right up there with key works by Haneke, Cronenberg, and Noé in its effortless ability to push the audience in directions it never thought it’d go. Presaging both our current true-crime obsession and the era of “elevated arthouse horror,” this shockingly audacious debut feature by John McNaughton (WILD THINGS, MAD DOG & GLORY), with its chilling, career-defining turn by Michael Rooker (AMC's THE WALKING DEAD, GUARDIANS OF THE GALAXY), has inspired multiple generations of filmmakers to go for the throat. In a voyeuristic style that does not judge, McNaughton’s camera glides around a few short weeks in the life of a drifter psychopath (Rooker) operating with amoral lizard-brain impunity as he mass-murders on the streets of Chicago. For shelter, Henry exploits the already-toxic living situation of ex-cellmate Otis (Tom Towles), who eventually follows him in animalistic killing sprees with execution methods and victims chosen at random to avoid detection. Meanwhile, Otis’ unsuspecting sister Becky (Tracy Arnold) comes to visit and mysteriously falls in love with the distant Henry. Amongst the gruesome, senseless violence, McNaughton fashions an impeccable three-hander hangout film: one of America’s greatest indies that also became a revolutionary genre-bender. HENRY is just as much in conversation with SEX, LIES, AND VIDEOTAPE as it is with THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE or DAWN OF THE DEAD, and the film’s shattering industrial music score sets the scene in its own incredible way. (BRET BERG) Presented by Dark Sky Films & AGFA

films.title: Honoring Walter Hill: Extreme Prejudice
films.synopsis: Join us to honor the legendary Walter Hill with a lifetime achievement award, and a special screening of EXTREME PREJUDICE and a conversation following the film.

films.title: Hyperreal Breakfast Club
films.synopsis: Austin’s Hyperreal Film Club recreates the childhood experience that shaped us all: eating breakfast in front of the TV before our parents woke up. Stop by the Highball for an immersive melange of spooky programs, complimentary coffee and cereal, goodie bags for early arrivals, and so much more. PJs optional.

films.title: I Have Proof
films.synopsis: If you look at James Cullen Bressack’s IMDb, you will see 51 directing credits and 196 producing credits. I don’t know how many films qualify for someone to be considered prolific, but at only 34 years old, either the kid just keeps slapping his name on shit or he legitimately never stops working! Either way, I HAVE PROOF is just that; proof that when Bressack steps away from the movie machine he has built, he is still able to tap into the filmmaker instincts that were present in his early career, regardless of the budget he is given to work with. I HAVE PROOF is a film made of pure rawness and grit. There is dirt on the lens, spit in each scene, and blood in the reels. And you will feel it. Bressack bought an assortment of old home video tapes, mostly because that is the only way you to find enough VHS-C tape at Bressack production speed, and wrapped the production just a few weeks after its inception. Each tape carried a ghost signal of what was once there; a flicker, a moan, a body, bleeding through the horror that was recorded over it. This movie is not for everyone. It is deeply disturbing, uncomfortable, and as visceral a gut punch as you could hope to get at a film festival. It totally fucking hits. This found footage, mostly POV film, is led by relative newcomers Larsen Deane and Lily Van der Meer, and frequent fixtures in the Bressack universe: B.J. Hendricks, Kay Day, and David Josh Lawrence. If you miss when found footage actually felt dangerous, this is for you. (AHBRA PERRY)

films.title: Into the Sky
films.synopsis: We first meet Bobby butt-naked, covered in blue goo, lying on a golf course in North Carolina, hundreds of miles away from his hometown in upstate New York. For the past year, Bobby's life has been shattered by repeated abductions at the hands of a mysterious force in the sky. After making his way back home, with his marriage now in shambles, he meets Nico. Nico is renting his former house while planning her brother's wedding, with the hope that it will prove to her family that she isn't a burnout. Unaware of the external forces disrupting Bobby's existence, Nico becomes entangled in his life as the two strike a deal to help solve each other's problems: Bobby will help plan the wedding, and Nico will help Bobby reconnect with his estranged wife. The arrival of Jaden, another abductee who has suffered the same bizarre phenomenon as Bobby for the past five years, only raises the stakes and adds to Bobby's problems. Beginning as an intriguing abduction mystery centered on Bobby's desperate attempts to understand what is happening to him, INTO THE SKY gradually reveals itself to be something more far out. Elevated by a solid ensemble including Sam Richardson, Sofia Black-D'Elia, and David Cross, the film refuses to stay grounded in a single genre. Combining a heartfelt romance, cosmic mystery, and light comedy, directors Drew Mylrea and Evan Wolf Buxbaum craft a genre mash-up that will lift its audience up into unexpected places. (RAFAEL RODRIGUEZ)

films.title: Janur Ireng: Sewu Dino the Prequel
films.synopsis: For anyone wondering precisely how many goat sacrifices are too many for one movie, Kimo Stamboel’s latest slice of blood-drenched Southeast Asian gothic horror does its damnedest to find out. Serving as a prequel to the Indonesian box office smash SEWU DINO (aka A THOUSAND DAYS), JANUR IRENG turns back the clock to 1997 to explore the origins of a debilitating thousand-day curse. Three months after the untimely death of their father, siblings Sabdo and Intan are left desperate and destitute when their family home mysteriously burns to the ground. Seemingly out of nowhere, Arjo, the wealthy uncle they never knew they had, appears and invites them to come and live at his palatial country estate. No sooner have they arrived, however, when Sabdo is forced to participate in bizarre late-night rituals, while his younger sister experiences all manner of supernatural disturbances as she is groomed for an even more nefarious fate. Stamboel, a long-time Fantastic Fest favorite who has been terrifying and delighting Texas crowds ever since his early collaborations with fellow Mo Brother, Timo Tjahjanto, pulls out all the stops for this deliriously demonic delight. As with all the best Indonesian horror films, things start off innocuous enough, with malformed shadows and unexplained bumps in the night, but it doesn’t take long until events crescendo into a cacophonous carnivale of giant horned demons, disembodied spirits, and ancient rituals, climaxing in an eruption of decapitations and disembowelments, as ancient folklore and timeless savagery collide in spectacular blood-soaked revelry. Adapted from much the same school of folklore-infused online creepypasta that nurtured successes like BACKROOMS and SLENDER MAN, JANUR IRENG weaves potent historical context into the origins of an already established mythology.

films.title: Jim Queen
films.synopsis: Jim Perfect is indeed perfect: perfect body, perfect hookups, perfect body hair distribution, and a perfectly monetized social media and OnlyFans presence. He’s the hottest guy in Paris, with a string of adoring fans begging just for a scrap of his attention. One of those adoring fans is Lucien, a tiny twink with a shrine to Jim in his bedroom closet, hidden away from the ever-watchful eyes of his conservative politician mother. When Jim is struck with heterotosis, the mysterious virus turning queer people all over France straight, he loses all his Instagram followers and is forced to team up with Lucien in an odyssey through gay Paris to find the cure. Nicolas Athane and Marco Nguyen’s animated satire skewers everyone from the gym gay who won’t get off his phone at the weight rack to the purist leather daddy who won’t take "no" for an answer. A world premiere in Cannes’ Midnighter section earlier this year, JIM QUEEN gleefully recreates queer male subcultures with a cheeky wink and a deep affection. Like a drag queen lovingly reading you for filth, this comedy can only be so mean to its subjects because it knows and loves them so thoroughly. The past couple of years have been really rough. In America and across the globe, we’ve witnessed a rising tide of far-right fascism sweep through politics and into our lives. While certainly not new, it has been turbocharged recently, and our queer family has been scapegoated and attacked on all sides. JIM QUEEN, with all its silliness, is a movie about the need for our community to come together to fight back against the oppression and the erasure of our queerness. Conservative fascism is here, and we will rise up to meet it with fetish singlets and rubber pups. (AUSTIN KING)

films.title: Jollyface
films.synopsis: Nick and Blair seem like the perfect couple. Sure, there are moments when Blair's desire to be a well-meaning ally veers into "white savior" territory, like when she urges Nick to confront what she perceives as judgmental looks directed at them for being a biracial couple. Nick seems to be accustomed to these interactions; he plays along, and life moves on. In his feature film debut, Justin Floyd crafts a home invasion horror film that uses familiar genre conventions to examine the ways racial identity can be manipulated and weaponized. As an exciting new voice in horror, the director is able to project an understanding of the contradictions, anxieties, and fears that exist within communities of color. Despite its complex themes, the movie never loses sight of its flow and its characters, allowing their emotional struggles to provide a balance to the escalating violent situations happening around them. The true terror of JOLLYFACE lies not only in its menacing villain but in the systems and attitudes that allow these kinds of monsters to exist. With contemporary, pointed social commentary, the film delivers kills, shocks, and uncomfortable truths, leaving audiences with plenty to discuss. (RAFAEL RODRIGUEZ)

films.title: Kick On
films.synopsis: Eden and her three best friends spend their nights drinking, dancing, getting high, and breaking into fights across Melbourne's club scene. They are kicked out of a dance club, and after a quick pit stop for a chicken souvlaki wrap and a few energy drinks, they set out in search of one last fix to keep the party going. Their night leads them to the extravagant drug lair of Roman, casually known to his friends as Ray, the volcanic son of a sadistic mobster. What begins as an awkward afterparty, fueled by a mountain of drugs, bad decisions, and Ray's increasingly reckless behavior, quickly spirals into a violent situation far beyond the group's casual bar fights. Trapped inside the apartment, Eden and her friends must fight for their lives to escape while paranoia, betrayal, and brutal violence continue to escalate between Ray and his gang. As a fan of Irish goodbyes, a bad party you can't escape from is one of my worst nightmares. KICK ON is far from your typical D.A.R.E. after-school special, delivering a drug-fueled crime thriller with enough gore, impalings, and relentless mayhem to rival the nastiest slashers. Director Nick Kozakis continues to cement himself as an original voice in the Australian Horror New Wave, blending razor-sharp pacing and an infectious sense of fun that never undercuts the brutality of the film. KICK ON shows how Australian genre cinema remains as wild, inventive, and unapologetic as ever. Fantastic Fest is thrilled to host the US Premiere of KICK ON. So, grab your mates; this is one party you won't want to miss. (RAFAEL RODRIGUEZ)

films.title: Kung Fu Deadly
films.synopsis: Danny and Frank, childhood best friends with mild boundary issues, are eking out a living in Dublin with their haphazardly run extermination company when they come across a group of Chinese criminals attempting to unleash a Jiangshi on the city with the Taoist guardian, Lien, currently hunting them. Lien quickly uncovers the fact that Danny is, by lineage, the other guardian that should be helping her; a fact he is blissfully unaware of in the tedium of his life. From deciding whether to hang up his branded coveralls and sell his childhood home to being tasked with protecting humanity, Danny’s life is at a major crossroads and Frank is along for the ride. The unlikely trio, as well as Danny and Frank’s auntie, set out to discover the truth about Danny’s father and the criminals spreading this evil, while convincing and training Danny to accept his destiny. For his sophomore feature outing, director Fergal Costello (WE ARE NOT ALONE) is joined by action director Lee Huang (WARRIOR NUN, THE MATRIX RESURRECTIONS) to create a hilarious, action-filled supernatural adventure. Bringing together young, up-and-coming actors in the lead roles and veteran stunt performers, KUNG FU DEADLY delivers heart, laughs, and, of course, dynamic fights to tell a fun, uplifting story about the power of friendship. (KEV DOOLEY)

films.title: Kylgor in the Grisly Abyss
films.synopsis: A nearly utopian kingdom secretly provides for its people by ravaging and oppressing neighboring lands. One day, one of those kingdoms elects a trio of champions and charges them with a simple task: kill the king. Kylgor and his men battle courageously through the kingdom, storm the castle, and promptly remove the king’s head before fleeing from his most faithful guards. While navigating their escape, Kylgor, his compatriots, and the king’s guards fall into a deep, mystical cave. Trapped, with only their wits and steel to save them from an unending horde of ravenous beasts, deceitful hallucinations, and evil magicks corrupting their very flesh (err… foam rubber), the former enemies must either find enough common ground to work together or die in the dark labyrinth. KYLGOR IN THE GRISLY ABYSS, the directorial debut from writer/director Mason Jeffrey Newton-DeRushie, is full of blood and guts, the nearly forgotten art of stop-motion animation, gnarly puppets, beautiful illustrations, and, above all, heart. In the tradition of the great sword-and-sandal barbarian movies, airbrushed conversion vans, and kids' movies that were way too heavy for their intended audience, KYLGOR IN THE GRISLY ABYSS delivers on every promise it makes. Mason Jeffrey Newton-DeRushie crafts deep lore and a world that I can’t wait to return to. (KEV DOOLEY) *Paired with the short GOODBYE, MONSTER dir. Luke Barnett You know what they say: a boy becomes a man the day the monster living under his bed decides it's time to go back to Hell. A FANGORIA Studios production featuring Patton Oswalt and Tina Majorino, scored by Bear McCreary.

films.title: Little Doors
films.synopsis: Isolated and awkward, a woman hires an equally socially inept locksmith to open a door in her empty, abandoned McMansion in the quiet post-apocalyptic world of LITTLE DOORS. A small connection built on mirroring behavior and unambiguous communication quickly becomes a relationship as he’s invited to move in. The two make every attempt at a normal romantic relationship, including uncomfortably standing by a fire together, exchanging gifts, having a picnic while the world burns behind them, and spending nearly every moment together while their conversations continue in their quiet, matter-of-fact manner. All the while, the woman is hiding a secret. A large, angry-looking cyst reveals itself to be a small, locked wooden door in the side of her body. A door someone starts knocking on from the other side. No longer able to hide it, the two face the decision of whether or not to open it. She explores medical and spiritual intervention to no avail, and eventually allows her partner to pick the lock. What they find on the other side transforms their relationship forever. A thoughtful, absurdist exploration of relationships, emotional availability, and one’s own sense of self, LITTLE DOORS quietly speaks volumes. Anthony Oberbeck, as writer, director, and co-lead of LITTLE DOORS, expertly weaves deadpan humor and heart while illuminating the sad, difficult realities of finding connection in the modern world. A powerful directorial debut, this movie has a unique charm that is sure to resonate with those of us who have a terminal case of social awkwardness. (KEV DOOLEY)

films.title: Magick Mtn.
films.synopsis: Lord Mmorke, a tepid and ghoulish narrator, walks us through 3 separate fables all intersecting in a realm beyond the tangible. Rituals and retellings about a Deathrock squatter jailed by a sadistic psychiatrist and the evils of regret, a pair of criminal plumbers plunging further towards Hell's grips and the beer-soaked leather of the Sunset Strip, and an architect's ambition built on the shaky bedrock of the Devil's promise. What begins as a tale ends in a spell cast upon unsuspecting characters and audiences alike. (HAL SATIN & HANA MAE LEE)

films.title: Monday Market
films.synopsis: Books, prints, and physical media galore! Get your goods and offerings from Ghoulish Bookfair, Retro Market, Mise en Scène, and other local artists. And remember, early birds get the bookworms.

films.title: Morning Meditation
films.synopsis: When does the movie end? Come and sit with certified meditation instructor, Hagy, for a mindful investigation of projectors watching projectors.

films.title: Mr. Creamjeans' Hidey Hole
films.synopsis: Keep your safe word handy as we follow blackmail victim Henry, guided by the dulcet tones of the eponymous Mr. Creamjeans, through the Hidey Hole, a “museo de arqueología erótica” unlike anything we’ve ever seen. The offer to Henry is simple: see what the Hidey Hole has to offer, provide his own contribution to the curation, and the tapes of whatever it is he has done will be his. What follows is a collection of bizarre, lewd vignettes, each more satisfying than the one before. From delivering what an underappreciated wife really wants to rejecting the notion of a single final girl in the name of sisterhood, MR. CREAMJEANS' HIDEY HOLE consistently provides gut-busting laughs and more phalluses than maybe all other feature film submissions to Fantastic Fest this year combined. MR. CREAMJEANS' HIDEY HOLE is a bold and unapologetic first feature from director Heath Benfield and writers Josh Griffey (Mr. Creamjeans himself) and Jonathan Holiday, who, along with other cast and crew, make up the film collective Misfit Parade. For the last several years, Misfit Parade have honed their skills and their “Troma, but elevated” sensibilities on a series of bawdy shorts, building a dedicated audience who shares their sense of humor and need to emasculate male entitlement. Don’t miss your opportunity to become a misfit and see this future cult classic first in its World Premiere at Fantastic Fest. (KEV DOOLEY) *Paired with the short TERMS & CONDITIONS dir. Kev Dooley A douchey techbro gets more than he bargained for when the genderqueer demon he used AI to summon sloughs off his control and sows chaos instead.

films.title: No Rest for the Wicked
films.synopsis: The Faroe Islands are a hard place to live. Daily life is a struggle, and everyone knows each other and their business. A young man, Baldur, chafes against the restrictions of his religiously conservative community, particularly when he is saved from a drowning accident by a very scruffy, intense stranger named Helge. Their burgeoning relationship is cut short by Christian judgment and tragedy, and all hope appears to be lost. A blood sacrifice to the unknown being who dwells beneath the waves brings renewed hope in this doomed, eldritch romance. NO REST FOR THE WICKED begins as many an indie gay romance does: a period piece, repressive religiosity, and lingering stares. Once the isolated, 19th-century community has been established and our two leads have begun to open up, the film takes a turn into unfathomable horror. It’s a refreshing shift in genre, emphasizing the mysteriousness of the ocean and the power of queer transgression. Fantastic Fest is a particularly unique festival where our audience can ignore standard models of morality and root for the gay man who makes a supernatural deal permitting possession and blood sacrifice. Egor Venned plays the young, inexperienced Baldur, and Pilou Asbæk (GAME OF THRONES’ Euron Greyjoy) is the confident, older sailor who helps Baldur to accept himself. NO REST FOR THE WICKED revels in unspeakable horror as a metaphor for the resistance to heterosexuality and the destruction of societal norms. If that sounds too heavy, have no fear; there's also a lot of hairy, sea-soaked chests and eldritch, bloody nipple play. (AUSTIN KING)

films.title: No Way Down
films.synopsis: Idriss is fresh out of prison and determined to leave his past behind, hoping to rebuild his life and reunite with his girlfriend, Mélia. When he visits a former associate to collect money he's owed, he's offered a deal instead: the debt will only be settled once Idriss evicts a squatter from the abandoned Kraken apartment complex. Refusing to be drawn back into violence, Idriss walks away. But the conversation is overheard by Ouss, an aspiring gangster eager to prove himself. Seeing an opportunity, Ouss decides to enter the Kraken and do the job himself. His friend Marvin, a self-proclaimed content creator, tags along, unaware that they are stepping into the territory of a dangerous and deeply violent man. When Mélia—Marvin's sister—learns where her brother is headed, she calls Idriss and begs him to help bring him back. As the group enters the vast, decaying complex in search of the boys, the tension steadily mounts. Climbing floor after floor, they come to realize they are being hunted by a man whose existence is intimately tied to Idriss's past. NO WAY DOWN marks the feature debut of Théo Jourdain and Mohamed Chabane, delivering a raw and brutal thriller. Their boogeyman emerges from a very real social issue affecting major cities around the world: the shortage of affordable housing and the ruthless practices sometimes employed to clear unwanted tenants. Bolstered by a talented young cast, Jourdain and Chabane turn the sprawling, decrepit Kraken complex into a nightmarish labyrinth, expertly trapping their characters alongside a relentless psychopath and ensuring the audience feels every ounce of the film's suffocating claustrophobia. (ANNICK MAHNERT)

films.title: Ogroff (Presented by Bleeding Skull)
films.synopsis: If Leatherface from THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE made a home movie with a Super 8 film camera, it would feel a lot like OGROFF. The French countryside is stalked by Ogroff, a deranged cannibal armed with a menagerie of knives, axes, and chainsaws. No one who enters Ogroff's haunted forest is safe from the killer's bloodthirsty wrath—not lumberjacks, automobiles, or children. One day, a woman (who may also be a serial killer) becomes obsessed with tracking down Ogroff. Will her infatuation lead to love or something far more sinister? Nothing else on earth resembles OGROFF. Shot on Super 8 film for $18,000 in France's Orléans Forest by video shop owner/horror zine publisher Norbert Moutier (aka N.G. Mount), this is the zenith of accidental avant-garde horror. Moutier applies his influences (Fulci's CITY OF THE LIVING DEAD, Hooper's THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE, Rollin's THE GRAPES OF DEATH) to a chaotic, droned-out slasher aesthetic that showcases experimental synthesizers, crazed gore, and surreal deviations from reality. Dizzying, fascinating, and charmingly nihilistic, OGROFF stands at the precipice of inspired art and lowbrow trash. But it transcends both as a singular mutation that you'll never forget. Now for the first time, Bleeding Skull presents a sparkling restoration of OGROFF from the newly discovered U-matic tape masters. Just don't get too close to the forest... you may never return. (Joseph A. Ziemba)

films.title: Opening Night Party!
films.synopsis: Join us for a raucous performance from Drakulas to kick off your fest! Drakulas started as a conceptual project that evolved into a cinematic synth-punk/new wave/garage rock band gang with members of storied punk bands Riverboat Gamblers and Rise Against. They’re tough guys from the sleazy, neon-lit streets of a late-70s fictionalized megacity raised on drugs, porn, the occult, video games, and underground art. “We Drakulas continue to evolve our sonic mastery of lo-fi instrumentation, the result of a dirty basement, menthol cigarettes and the warm glow of a cathode ray TV. We spilled kerosene on the keyboards to make them sound uglier. Not for squares.”

films.title: Out of the Crypt!
films.synopsis: Join hostess, Louisianna Purchase and her cast of ghouls, as they serve creature feature drag! Louisianna will test your monster knowledge with contests for special, event-only prizes!

films.title: Pathetic Fallacy
films.synopsis: Asher and Iris are madly in love. After Iris succumbs to cancer, Asher is wracked with grief, searching for answers, wishing he had been taken instead of her. In his quest to reconnect with her, he stumbles into an alternate universe filled with homicidal maniacs, talking creatures, and one very cool dive bar. He’s given a tempting offer: try to cheat death and bring her back… but at what cost? Director Adam Egypt Mortimer (DANIEL ISN’T REAL, ARCHENEMY) is no stranger to crafting mind-bending tales, and he’s brought the full force of his talent to crafting PATHETIC FALLACY. Wildly imaginative and incredibly touching, the film is filled with psychedelic visuals and propulsive action, all shot on 35mm. Anchoring the film are incredible performances from Jessica Rothe and Scott “Kid Cudi” Mescudi, whose onscreen chemistry is palpable. The two also lend their vocal talents to the incredible soundtrack by Johnny Jewel, which serves as the backbone of the film. PATHETIC FALLACY is by turns exhilarating, heartbreaking, hilarious—and most of all, human. (LISA DREYER)

films.title: Phreaker
films.synopsis: AT&T poisoned the minds of millions by telling them to “reach out and touch someone.” What did they expect from those grasping for human connection? For Jake Bellman, a blind teenager in a downwardly mobile home at the turn of the 21st century, the phone became a curiosity and then an obsession. He finds himself in chat rooms, striking up conversations with strangers, only to discover that he has a gift for mimicry. By memorizing dial tones, he can swindle systems into free long-distance calls, and by imitating those on the other end of the line, he can manipulate to a far greater degree. It’s called “phreaking,” and Jake is one of the best to ever do it. This, however, is a recipe for making more enemies than friends. Picking up the baton from hacker classics like SNEAKERS and THE SOCIAL NETWORK, Adam Yorke’s sophomore feature delivers a taut, propulsive character piece in a world before pre-digital ubiquity. Based on true events, with the names changed to protect the innocent (and the guilty), PHREAKER is one that you can’t miss. (JAKE ISGAR)

films.title: Platypus
films.synopsis: A woman receives a foreboding tarot reading. A man eating an apple is murdered on a beach. A precocious young woman has dreams of a masked killer. A woman walks into an antique store followed by a mysterious figure... and the film continues. Describing the plot of PLATYPUS is like trying to explain a slasher captured through a dream. Sexual desire, violence, voice-over, a plot unconcerned with character arc, and obviously fake blood are just a few of the elements that make up Joshua Gratton’s second feature outing as a director. A beautifully constructed throwback, PLATYPUS transcends a mere love letter to a genre and celebrates the joys of low-budget, DIY filmmaking. Each kill, each cut around an actor starting a movement cue, and each bit of ridiculous dialogue draws your attention to the movie being brought to life in front of you. You will see nothing else this year—at Fantastic Fest at least, but I would bet all year long—like PLATYPUS. Wholly original, laugh-out-loud funny, and strangely disturbing, this relatively simple horror premise feels like trying to remember a movie that never existed. Shot on Super 8 film and accompanied by one of the best scores of the year, each moment feels ripped from half a dozen low-rent movies you’d catch on cable at 2 AM. Gratton’s film indulges in the sensual pleasures of the genre (stay away if full-frontal nudity isn’t your jam), demonstrating his familiarity with the tropes while queering them at every turn. It’s a heady concoction that creates a film that feels transgressive and incredibly familiar, especially for a Fantastic Fest audience. So grab your mask, a knife, and your stupidest, hot boyfriend for the World Premiere of PLATYPUS. (AUSTIN KING) *Paired with the short FUCK FACE dir.

films.title: Play House
films.synopsis: Exactly one year ago, Nic Curcio, Kirby Gladstein, and Ben Gojer stood on stage in the Highball and promised all of us that they could make a kick-ass horror film. They won the inaugural Fantastic Pitches and have returned to Fantastic Fest to world premiere PLAY HOUSE. Since accepting their crowns, the team has been on a full sprint to the finish. With no time to catch their breath, the team barreled through development, casting, and production, taking a week's break for the director and producer to get married before heading into post. Divide/Conquer (M3GAN, BLACK PHONE 2) joined Chroma as executive producers on the film. My spidey senses and my Instagram algorithm tell me that this is just the beginning of what will be very scary and successful careers for all three of these champions. Curcio’s directorial debut follows Elliot (Will Harrison from DAISY JONES & THE SIX) as he navigates a terror where all millennial egos go to die: the real estate market, where thanks to the death of his mother, he is able to buy the most shitty of homes in LA County. With the help of his best friend Alden (Jordan Gonzalez from THE LONG WALK), Elliot plans to restore the dilapidated house to the cozy home it once was in hopes of winning back his ex-girlfriend played by Jessica Sula (MICHAEL), because nothing says emotional growth like the grand gesture of home-buying. While cleaning out the basement of his new home, Elliot discovers some old VHS tapes crammed into the dark reaches of the broken water heater. Each musty tape contains an episode of a children’s television show that not even the darkest nerd corners of the internet can identify. The show’s host Mr. Morton (James Urbaniak from OPPENHEIMER) smiles with the kind of warmth that curdles a few seconds too late, and his monster friends feel less like puppets than something that used to be.

films.title: Posthumous
films.synopsis: Zoe's drinking has become a problem, so she's abandoned her car, her boyfriend and temporarily moved back in with her surly, widower father—a man who's content to share meals and pay off her drunk driving fines, but seems to have little interest in emotionally connecting with his daughter. Zoe's mother died from a terminal illness after rejecting life-saving treatment that could have compromised her pregnancy, but before she departed, she had the foresight to leave behind a series of VHS recordings—concise messages of motherly wisdom meant to be viewed annually on Zoe's birthdays up to her 21st. Resigned to the couch while her father's at work, Zoe spends her 30th birthday alone, rewatching the old VHS tape, charting her mother's decline from grainy message to grainy message, aware that her relationship with her mother has always been a one-way conversation through physical media that degrades a little bit every time she pops the tape into the family VCR. When a new lead points Zoe to the reclusive widow next door, and her father gets evasive about their shared past, Zoe breaks in and uncovers a failed occult therapy to channel her mother's pain through portals opened by arcane sacred geometry... and possibly, a way to finally converse with her mother through those same cracks. Director Josh Tanner's debut feature is a chilling ghost story, with some genuinely creepy chills, twists, and jumps, but what stuck with me after the credits rolled was how thoughtfully Tanner uses Zoe's mother's analog VHS recordings to stand in for memory itself—subjectively captured and slowly wearing down each time it's revisited. (CHRIS LARSEN)

films.title: PowerPints
films.synopsis: Drink and learn things at PowerPints, the Original, 2 time Best of Austin nominated comedy show where presenters deliver a PowerPoint on any weird, fascinating, niche subject they like in five minutes or less, otherwise they suffer the consequences of a spicy pickle shot! Previous topics have included 'Blucifer & Denver's Freaky Ass Airport's Secrets', 'Why I Trust Horror Movies Over RomComs', 'We Need To Talk About Duo: A Scientific Violence Risk Assessment of the DuoLingo Mascot', and 'The Mystery of the Montauk Monster'. What will tonight’s subjects include? Show up to find out!

films.title: Primetime
films.synopsis: In 2006, To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history.

films.title: Red Snow
tags: Girls Just Want to Have Fun
films.synopsis: Johanna is a rebellious teenager whose parents are divorced. Her mother doesn't really want to spend time with her, her father is too preoccupied with his upcoming wedding to his new girlfriend, and her little brother is a brat. Johanna's only wish is to become a vampire, like Edward in TWILIGHT, to escape her miserable life. On Christmas night, the whole family drives to her grandmother's house for the holiday—an eccentric woman who lives in a huge mansion. When Santa shows up at the door and asks for permission to enter, all hell breaks loose: he's actually a vampire on a rampage. To Johanna's delight, her wish might finally come true. But every vampire has an enemy, and when a hunter arrives at the house with his psychopathic apprentice, he unleashes havoc, turning the entire night into a nightmare. Suddenly, becoming a vampire doesn't seem as appealing as Johanna once thought. RED SNOW is Ilja Rautsi's first feature. Mostly known for his work as a screenwriter on HATCHING and NIGHTBORN, he made a name for himself directing two outrageous short films that traveled festivals worldwide: HELSINKI MANSPLAINING MASSACRE and NIGHT OF THE LIVING DICKS. If you don't know the man, his ice-cold Finnish humor and demeanor may put you off, but under that cold Nordic exterior is a huge genre fan and talented director who twists genre conventions to deliver outrageously dark comedic stories that will make you giggle in your seat. And in these somber times we live in, we certainly need outrageous dark comedy. (ANNICK MAHNERT)

films.synopsis: From the mind of visionary filmmaker Zach Cregger (WEAPONS, BARBARIAN) comes a thrilling — and terrifying — reinvention of the RESIDENT EVIL franchise. In an all-new story, RESIDENT EVIL follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos. From TriStar Pictures, Constantin Film, and Davis Films, RESIDENT EVIL hits theatres September 18, 2026. (TRISTAR PICTURES)

films.title: River
films.synopsis: After the death of their father, Carla, Drew, and Lucy reunite to scatter his ashes on the river he loved so much. Their relationship is clearly strained, and tension mounts when Carla speeds the boat up and strikes something just beneath the surface, causing a fuel leak. Old wounds are torn open and the blame game ensues, making it painfully clear their father was far from perfect. Stranded on the river and with no obvious way back, Carla takes matters into her own hands, swimming toward shore with a plan to walk back to the car. But as she nears the bank, she spots a bloodied, masked man watching her from the tree line. She swims back to the boat in a panic... and the man follows. Setting aside their grievances becomes the siblings' only hope of survival, as a lunatic with no intention of letting them leave begins to play a merciless game of cat and mouse. You have to hand it to Joshua Giuliano for a remarkable opening scene, one that toys with the audience's imagination from the very first frame. Setting the tone within the first five minutes is merely the starting point of a descent into hell for these three characters. By placing them on a boat—isolated and vulnerable—Giuliano forges a new kind of hunting ground for a psychopathic killer, ensuring the audience is given no moment of relief. And this is only the beginning. Superbly shot and anchored by stellar performances across the board, RIVER is a film that will stay with you long after the credits roll. For a debut feature, Giuliano delivers one of the most terrifying films of the year—and whatever he does next, he has set a formidably high bar for himself. (ANNICK MAHNERT)

films.title: Roma Elastica
films.synopsis: No one does it like our boy Mandico. His post-apocalyptic fever dream AFTER HOURS stole hearts in 2022; his queer fantasy epic SHE IS CONANN tore ‘em apart in 2023; his daring split-screen dance picture DRAGON DILATATION caused many an aggressive chin stroke. With ROMA ELASTICA, he sets his gaze toward the lineage of Italian cinema with this retro-kitsch blast… in English, no less! Marion Cotillard, herself no stranger to Fantastic Fest after last year’s THE ICE TOWER and 2015’s APRIL AND THE EXTRAORDINARY WORLD, is Eddie: a capital-M Movie Star who may be at the end of her illustrious career. Maybe it’s the burn from international success; maybe it’s the cancer metastasizing inside of her—who’s to say? Wooed to Rome for a brazen French/Italian co-production, Eddie and her gal Friday (a very game Noémie Merlant) dive headfirst into the future, as only a high-powered 1980s mega-production could deliver. With a body of work about shifting and parallel fantasies, it’s no surprise that Mandico would eventually set his sights on cinema itself. And with Cotillard’s ferocious performance, he has the perfect vessel for exploring this dream space with equally gorgeous and complex interiority. An instant entry into the Movie-About-Movies Hall of Fame, ROMA ELASTICA is a pure pleasure object, hitting at the surface and burrowing far underneath. #MANDICO4EVA (JAKE ISGAR)

films.title: Roy from Space
films.synopsis: Roy is an astronaut on a mission to Mars. He quickly uncovers a scheme to invade Earth from an evil space empire and, with his girlfriend and his spaceship’s doctor, he must put a stop to the villainous plot before time runs out. ROY FROM SPACE was released in 1983 to a somewhat confused reaction. Directed by Héctor López Carmona with a very small budget and a small team of animators, many of whom had never professionally animated previously, there definitely are some rough edges. The film was heavily criticized for its jerky animations and a plot that seemed to float from event to event with little connective tissue. Roy and his fellow spacefarers populate a colorful, hyperpop world that operates on the logic of a B-movie 1960s space opera. While perhaps not hard sci-fi, there is a certain science-fiction/fantasy enthusiasm that infects every frame. ROY FROM SPACE plays like a three-episode arc of a Saturday morning Space Race cartoon, at least in this programmer’s opinion. Originally the film contained a section lifted from a Japanese sci-fi film that someone… forgot… to get the rights to, and the animators had also traced over sections of the original 1936 FLASH GORDON serial. For 43 years, the film was abandoned to the halls of cinema obscurity. No longer. Featuring a newly animated section to replace the Japanese footage, and with a blessing from the daughter of the film’s original producer, Deaf Crocodile has restored this gem of Mexican cinema to be enjoyed in all its glorious retro-futurist wonder. ROY FROM SPACE is perfect for you if you love ‘60s STAR TREK or Spaceman Spiff. (AUSTIN KING) *Paired with the short LIL GIBBOS | HOT DROP dir. Arius Ziaee When a perennially lazy sack of shit decides to try hot yoga, the sentient microorganisms living on his body experience the marvels of sweat for the very first time.

films.title: Screamplay
films.synopsis: Edgar Allan (Rufus Butler Seder) is an aspiring screenwriter who has just come to Hollywood to make it in the movies... only to wind up working as the janitor at a fleabag apartment complex run by the greasy ex-boxer Martin (George Kuchar) instead. When Edgar begins channeling his frustrations with his kooky neighbors into fodder for his latest screenplay, the vivid murder scenes he writes begin to happen for real. As the bodies pile up and the line between reality and fiction becomes increasingly blurred, Edgar, convinced that the only way to be a real writer is to suffer, is slowly driven mad. Inventively produced using a host of early cinematic techniques and featuring a memorable performance by underground film legend George Kuchar, Rufus Butler Seder's SCREAMPLAY is a singularly charming tribute to Old Hollywood and a marvel of low-budget but high-concept filmmaking. New 4K restoration by Muscle Distribution in association with Matchbox Cine. (ELIZABETH PURCHELL)

films.title: Short Fuse
films.synopsis: Our signature block of horror shorts offers fifty flavors of fright and then some! From bizarro birthday parties to sapphic slasher sleepovers and backyard exorcisms, there’s a buffet of frightening fun to be had here. But look out: monsters abound — stalking the beaches of Senegal and rainforests of Malaysia, lurking in the darkened corners of camcorder footage, and following us into bed for a fitful (and frightening) night’s sleep. So, here, take this vape...it's dangerous to go alone! *Please note: films listed in alphabetical order, not in order of appearance in the block. BAGMAN- Dir. Connor Gaston & Vaughn Gaston Don’t you want to know what’s inside the bag? The “safe distance” afforded by screens sets a supernatural trap in this creepypasta-esque techno chiller from Canada. DËMM- Dir. Aida Captijn This beautifully captured Senegalese folk horror processes a girl's grief into a feeling of primeval terror. GIGIT - Dir. Farah Jabir Ten-year-old Din, frustrated with her gender and at war with Rambo, her harsh older brother, finds a dark kindred spirit in the form of the Pontianak — a vengeful female ghost out of Malaysian folklore. THE HAUNTING OF PLAY HOUSE - Dir. Chris McInroy The team behind CHÄIR, SKEETER, WE JOINED A CULT, and GUTS returns once again, this time with a priest summoned to exorcise a demonic playhouse. IT HELPS - Dir. John Zachary Thurman When Spencer turns off her brother’s trusted vintage white noise machine, she soon finds out that getting enough beauty sleep is the least of his worries. SCISSORS - Dir. Hannah Alline A violent man on a petty revenge quest gets more than he could've possibly prepared for when he enters a den of queer baddies. STRETCHER - Dir. Thibault Fauconnet A woman’s neck injury becomes an exercise in protracted cinematic cruelty in this slow-burning, fixed-camera shocker from France. TRANSFERENCE - Dir.

films.title: Shorts With Legs
films.synopsis: You are cordially invited to our meticulously curated WTF block. Your discerning eyes and ears shall be graced by unorthodox birthings, forbidden desires, anthropomorphized bodily fluids, and dark cosmic dystopias. These artistic emissaries from six nations bring the best of strange cinema, now and forever imprinted upon your malleable psyche. *Please note: films listed in alphabetical order, not in order of appearance in the block. BLESSING - Dir. Francisco Lacerda The demented mind behind last year’s YAZZA returns with a much more somber — dare we say it — hopeful take on self-destruction. DOG MOM - Dir. Diogo Hausen A shower goes to the dogs when a woman claims to have given actual live birth to her fur baby. Pets are literally family in this delightfully absurd ode to dog parents everywhere. EE - Heather Landsman How far would you go for a collectible anime figurine? This seductively crafted erotic thriller answers that, and more, in gloriously nostalgic MiniDV. A LOBSTER NAMED DESIRE - Dir. Sol Moreno & Risseth Yanguez Welcome to Cevicheria Afrodita, a seafood eatery for “sad, would-be lovers.” When her date rejects her favorite meal, Conchita takes her decapodic dish to go and winds up in a surreal situation involving humanoid crustaceans and intravaginal punk rock musical numbers. THE OLD LADY AND THE ETERNITY - Marc Martínez Jordán Spunky 86-year-old Josefa refuses to have her consciousness uploaded to a digital afterlife in this futuristic comedy. The filmmaker marries archival footage of his own late grandmother with generative AI to investigate the tensions and contradictions between image and self. ORLA - Dir. Marie Lukáčová A young maiden is banished by a tyrannical ruler to a mysterious faraway land from which no one has ever returned.

films.title: Sick
films.synopsis: A teenage boy is exiled to the countryside, tasked with caring for his ailing grandmother. Alone, he spends his days aimlessly scrolling Instagram, trying to get up the courage to text a girl he has a crush on. When his older sister shows up to help him, it’s a relief, as he now has company, as well as someone to help care for grandma. Relief quickly turns to annoyance as his sister begins teasing him, pushing his boundaries, and refusing to assist with their grandma’s care. What begins as a typical sibling dynamic slowly spirals into something much more complex, mirroring the transformation of their grandmother, who goes from lying comatose in bed to acting in extremely unusual and alarming ways. You may recognize Agata Trzebuchowska from her acting career (including the Academy Award-winning IDA), but her first feature puts her on the map as an exciting new director to watch. Fully in command of her craft, Trzebuchowska has created a fearless film, with impeccable sound design, beautiful cinematography, and impressive performances from the entire cast. The story unfolds subtly, slowly escalating, rewarding (or perhaps punishing) the viewer with my personal favorite ending of the fest. As the title implies, SICK is thrillingly perverse, which is the highest compliment at Fantastic Fest! (LISA DREYER)

films.title: The Birthday Party
films.synopsis: It’s been a big day for Nora. She got promoted, fought with her daughter about a viral reel she posted of the family dancing, and most importantly, tonight is her 40th birthday. She lives in the remote countryside with her husband, Thomas, and daughter, Ida, sharing the estate with Cristina, an artist neighbor busy painting works no one ever buys. But the evening doesn’t go as planned when three men arrive uninvited, claiming Nora is not who she says she is. Nora was expecting cake. Instead, she got served a slice of her unsavory past. Night falls, and we are suddenly thrust into a heady mix of power games, shifting loyalties, and false appearances. Nora fights to protect the identity she has built, Cristina enters into her own dangerous confrontation with one of the men, and Ida begins to question the family story she has taken for granted. Who is telling the truth? Do we even want to know? Beneath the appearances, the women are never truly passive. They observe, strategize, change the rules of the game, and fight to shape the lives they have chosen for themselves. Léa Mysius gifts us with another film exploring female subjectivity and secrets through genre, continuing the fascinating path she began with AVA and THE FIVE DEVILS. We are far more interested in its shifting identities and alliances than in simply finding out who will make it through the night. We are here for the clammy, uncanny, obsessive mood, and for the pleasure of watching identities crumble under pressure to reveal what survives—or blooms—from the wreckage. It is difficult to single out one performance from such an exceptional cast (Monica Bellucci, Hafsia Herzi, and Benoît Magimel, among others), but newcomer Tawba El Gharchi is incandescent. (SONIA DROULHIOLE)

films.title: The Blood Countess
films.synopsis: Countess Elizabeth Báthory awakens in the modern day with her devoted lover as the leader of an ancient organization of centuries-old vampires. When the group realizes that anti-vampire activists are on the hunt for a mystical book that could end their eternal lives, Elizabeth and her lover agree to find and destroy it first. With Elizabeth’s reluctant nephew, a committed vegetarian vampire, the three will travel across Austria meeting a whole cast of silly characters, exploring 21st-century life, and draining beautiful women of their blood. Isabelle Huppert plays vampire Elizabeth Báthory in a gloriously camp comedy from the legendary director, Ulrike Ottinger. I’m not sure what else you need to know to be sold on this, but allow me to try and convince you further. The lesbian subtext of Báthory’s biography is made text, Huppert’s character is accompanied by an adorable pet bat, and there’s a surprise, third-act cameo that brought the house down in my screening. Ottinger has made a name for herself as a writer/director with a deep love of arthouse cinema that she consistently and good-naturedly ribs. Her Isabelle Huppert vampire movie is no different, and the 84-year-old filmmaker brought her quirky sensibility to the lesbian vampire genre with appropriate flair: the costumes are over the top with ruffles and the blood sprays like geysers. There is, blessedly, no winking self-awareness to the jokes in this blood-soaked comedy as the ridiculous premise and characters are played ‘seriously.’ As such, this is high camp, so girls and gays to the front for the North American premiere of THE BLOOD COUNTESS. (AUSTIN KING)

films.title: The Cycle
films.synopsis: When the body of a man missing for thirty-six years is discovered at the scene of a horrific crime, it’s up to his estranged daughter to unravel his dark past. (SHUDDER)

films.title: The Face of Horror
films.synopsis: Ah, first love. Eleanor loves Edward. Edward loves her beautiful face, her gorgeous body, her money too, for sure. Her as a person? Probably not. And as for her father, certainly not at all. Which is why he kills him to secure Eleanor’s hand in marriage. Meanwhile, Edward’s squire murders the husband of Eleanor’s sister, Beatrice, to satisfy his obsessive lust. So when the two grief-stricken sisters agree to the marriages, they make one condition: that their father and Beatrice’s husband be avenged—unbeknownst to them, by the very men who murdered them. Marriage, however, does not live up to Edward’s childish, entitled notions of romance. He recoils from anything resembling responsibility: the farm, his sick wife, their child. He quickly redirects his affections toward a lovely, spoiled noblewoman who also happens to be significantly richer. He’s a knight, for god’s sake. He deserves luxury. And once Eleanor stands between him and the life he believes he is owed, he begins reluctantly, then increasingly enthusiastically, to arrange her destruction. He cannot stand her “sad face” anymore. Eleanor thus discovers that the man she loved never truly saw her as anything more than a pretty possession. Her marriage has become a nightmare. Luckily for her, death is not quite the end. Transposing the classic Japanese ghost story Yotsuya Kaidan to medieval England, Anna Biller once again builds a gorgeous romantic fantasy only to reveal the cruelty festering underneath. Shot on 35mm and drenched in vibrant color, THE FACE OF HORROR is campy, grotesque, frequently funny, and genuinely tragic. Edward may be absurd, but Eleanor’s suffering never is. (SONIA DROULHIOLE)

films.title: The Glorious Dead
films.synopsis: Sheriff Deb is woken up by her deputy, Mikey, on her day off. Half the sheriff's office hasn't shown up for work, and the phone lines are down. Deb heads out to perform a welfare check on a local resident, only to find the house completely empty. As the day unfolds, strange things begin happening around town. The power is out, blood runs from some faucets, animals have disappeared, and more and more people are reported missing. Residents are growing uneasy after discovering rotten, flesh-like holes on their properties. As the hours pass, things become increasingly bizarre. The dead come back to life, grotesque flesh-covered creatures begin roaming the town and feeding on people, and a heavy snowfall slowly engulfs the area. While Deb tries to make sense of what's happening, the remaining townspeople become convinced that a virus is spreading. They cut off all access in and out of town and begin burning the dead who have come back to life. Alone against the growing panic, Deb starts to realize that this strange and terrifying day may be the beginning of the end. It wouldn't be Fantastic Fest without our yearly dose of the Adams family. The most prolific family in genre filmmaking returns with their own take on the Rapture, setting the apocalypse not in a sprawling city but in a quiet small town, making it all the more unsettling. This isn't the end of the world you expect. It arrives quietly, spreads relentlessly, and before long has you by the throat. Every film the Adams family directs and produces feels different, yet unmistakably their own. THE GLORIOUS DEAD may be modest in scale, but it's generous in heart. And it's always a pleasure to see an entire family come together, film after film and year after year, with the same passion and commitment.

films.title: The Heretiks
films.synopsis: From Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski, the writers of HELLRAISER (2022) and THE NIGHT HOUSE, comes the first production from Dread Central’s new company Be Afraid—THE HERETIKS. Directed by Gregg Bishop, this Halloween-set home invasion horror fuses supernatural mayhem, suspense, and old-school practical-effects energy into one wickedly entertaining ride. Set over the course of a single fateful night, THE HERETIKS follows a disaffected teenager, Ada, forced into an unlikely alliance with a renegade witch when her younger sister, Mabel, is marked for sacrifice by a fanatical coven determined to usher in the apocalypse. As the clock races toward midnight, ancient grudges, forbidden magic, and blood-soaked rituals collide in a relentless fight for survival. The film channels the kinetic spirit of '80s horror while delivering a contemporary coming-of-age story about family, identity, and the courage to defy inherited beliefs. Bishop blends inventive scares, dark humor, and propulsive action to tell a tale that is as emotionally grounded as it is gleefully unhinged. Fueled by a fresh ensemble cast and an atmosphere steeped in autumnal dread, THE HERETIKS embraces the pleasures of practical horror without sacrificing heart. Every chase, spell, and confrontation builds toward a feverish finale that transforms Halloween night into a battleground between blind devotion and hard-won self-determination. Equal parts witchcraft thriller, survival horror, and midnight crowd-pleaser, the film is an exhilarating celebration of rebellious outsiders, supernatural chaos, and the enduring appeal of horror that wears its love of the genre proudly on its sleeve. (SARA LOPO)

films.title: The Kingcast
films.synopsis: Longtime friend of the fest Eric Vespe, with co-host Anthony Breznican, dive into all things Stephen King-related, with a special guest during this live podcast recording.

films.title: The Ones Who Grieve
films.synopsis: Set in the French countryside at the end of the 19th century, THE ONES WHO GRIEVE follows Jacob, a deeply religious man who works as a soul keeper. Believing he is liberating those afflicted by a mysterious illness, he imprisons them behind wooden masks after sewing their eyes and mouths shut. His daughter, Zélie, lives under his tyrannical rule and dreams of freedom. When Jacob sells her beloved horse, Thunder, her resentment reaches its breaking point, prompting her to defy him by hiding an infected soldier in the family barn. After Zélie is assaulted by a neighbor, Jacob's delusions deepen. Convinced she has sinned, he brutally mutilates her before deciding the only way to keep her "safe" is to keep her for himself. But Zélie has finally reached her limit. When an opportunity presents itself, she seizes it and turns the tables on her father. THE ONES WHO GRIEVE is French director Quarxx's third feature film. In 2018, he left a lasting impression on our audience with ALL THE GODS IN THE SKY, a bleak and unsettling science fiction tale. Although the two films differ in genre, they share a common thread: an unflinching exploration of suffering. With THE ONES WHO GRIEVE, Quarxx examines the tyranny of a self-proclaimed prophet who wields religion as a tool of domination and control. Thierry Frémont fully inhabits the role, delivering a chilling performance that lays bare the character's monstrous nature. (ANNICK MAHNERT)

films.title: The Spiral
films.synopsis: Meet Alice. Her estranged mother, Anna, has just arrived at her Rome apartment in the middle of a storm with a preposterous confession: twenty years ago, she made a bargain that cursed their entire family. Talk about dramatic. Back then, during a lavish party at the family estate, the family dog viciously attacked young Alice, crushing the dreams Anna had already built for her daughter. You see, she’d just booked her first commercial (for a pasta company). And in Anna’s mind, that future could not possibly survive the loss of a leg. So when a mysterious Stranger appears in the hospital chapel and offers Anna a one-of-a-kind bargain, however morally obscene, Anna refuses—until she doesn’t. Over the next two decades, every attempt she makes to repair the damage only creates new debts, new sacrifices, and consequences for the whole family—and beyond. The monster she fed once keeps demanding payment. Now, Anna believes Alice might hold the key to ending this cruel spiral. This is horror built from guilt: however much Anna loves her daughter, that love is contaminated by ambition, vanity, and the future she projected onto her. Fantastic Fest alum Paolo Strippoli returns with a lush, unnerving film. As in his previous work, he remains fascinated by the hidden costs of miracles and the moral cost of asking others to carry our pain. He also has a particular gift for turning seemingly ordered lives inside out, revealing the guilt and darker desires concealed beneath them. Jasmine Trinca and Romana Maggiora Vergano immerse us in this terrible night, while Valeria Bruni Tedeschi’s Stranger—charming, frightening, and utterly implacable—gives the film its most unsettling presence. Now do me a favor: however tempting, try to resist making bargains in churches. (SONIA DROULHIOLE)

films.title: The Squirrel
films.synopsis: In a futuristic, aseptic Finland where all forms of interaction and emotion are forbidden, Pasi, an engineer at Syn Bio working on a robotic dog, stumbles upon a strange creature at his way home. His personal AI assistant immediately alerts the sanitary department, and an agent is dispatched to investigate, only to find nothing. Later that night, Pasi returns to the spot and discovers a small injured squirrel. That might not seem unusual—if animals hadn't completely vanished from their world. Curious, Pasi brings the squirrel to work to have it scanned before taking it home, initially treating it like a biohazard. But contact with the tiny furry creature awakens something he has never experienced before: emotions. As his bond with the squirrel deepens, Pasi's entire world is turned upside down. THE SQUIRREL is Markus Lehmusruusu's second feature, and it's impossible not to be charmed by it. Pasi begins the story as a bored robotics engineer developing a mechanical substitute for a beloved pet—one designed to provide companionship without provoking any emotional attachment. Yet the more time he spends with the squirrel, the more curious he becomes and the more attached he grows. But squirrels have needs too, and Pasi eventually realizes that returning his tiny friend to where it belongs is the right thing to do—even if it means challenging everything he has been taught since birth. The film's production design is fantastic. Its chilly aesthetic and deadpan humor inevitably evoke Aki Kaurismäki, yet beneath the cold exterior lies a surprisingly warm story about resisting conformity and stepping beyond one's comfort zone. More than anything, THE SQUIRREL reminds us that life is richer when shared with animals. (ANNICK MAHNERT) *Paired with the short FIGHT FOR THE FANTASY dir.

films.title: The Swallow
films.synopsis: Five teenagers enter a chained-off section of a forest for a lazy weekend swimming in a river. There are some strange warnings around and a pile of muddy gear left behind by previous campers, but that probably means nothing, right? They don’t have cell service, but who cares? These teens are reconnecting with nature. Even setting up shelter seems unnecessary when you have all weekend. Unless this is your first horror movie ever, you can see where this is going. Shortly after arriving, the group comes across a strange toxic sludge that acts like quicksand with some extra, surprise quirks. That’s when they start dying. Are you afraid of the woods? Have you ever been dragged on a trip with your sister’s annoying, colossally stupid friends? Do you like watching young, beautiful people dying while covered in mud? THE SWALLOW is perfect for you. Kevin Kölsch and Dennis Widmyer’s genre construction feels like an intentional throwback to B-movies of the ‘80s with some modern anxieties. What does it mean to willingly abandon the comfort of the constant surveillance of a consistent WiFi connection? And can we ever know what forces are controlling our lives? THE SWALLOW doesn’t set out to answer these questions, even when it asks them, but it does kill some young people for your sadistic pleasure. Enjoy! (AUSTIN KING)

films.title: Too Many Beasts
films.synopsis: After being transferred to a small town in the French countryside for assaulting a superior officer, disgraced cop Orsini has all but given up on his career, going through the motions with little interest in the job. That changes when he and his new partner are called to investigate a series of acts of property damage across several estates. After hearing that the incidents may have been orchestrated by a local farmer long believed to be dead, Orsini begins digging deeper. As he gradually pieces the puzzle together, Orsini also begins opening up to the station psychiatrist, Stéphane Denjir, who proves to be just as troubled and disillusioned as he is. The deeper Orsini digs, the more he uncovers a web of corruption tied to the region's exploding wild boar population and its prestigious hunting season. As devastated crops fuel growing resentment among local farmers, long-simmering tensions threaten to erupt. With nothing left to lose and fed up with the corruption surrounding him, Orsini risks everything to expose the truth, aided by the equally determined Denjir. Inspired by an article in a French newspaper about farmers’ anger over supplemental wildlife feeding and the wild boar population explosion, Italian-Swiss filmmaker Sarah Arnold’s debut feature deftly blends offbeat black comedy with crime drama, while remaining firmly rooted in the very real conflict between social classes. Alexis Manenti and Ella Rumpf (whom our audience will recognize from RAW and TIGER GIRL) make for a perfectly mismatched duo whose chemistry reaches its peak in an outrageously funny final act. TOO MANY BEASTS, which premiered at the Directors' Fortnight in Cannes earlier this year, showcases the undeniable talent of a filmmaker with a masterful command of a cinematic language that seamlessly blends social satire with gleefully trashy humor. (ANNICK MAHNERT)

films.title: Upiro
tags: Girls Just Want to Have Fun
films.synopsis: Spain, 1755. As the Age of Enlightenment promises to replace superstition with reason, Ana, a young woman sent to a remote monastery to atone for her sins, finds herself trapped within a cloistered world ruled by unwavering faith and absolute obedience. Behind the convent's austere walls, several sisters are afflicted by a mysterious blood disease, while an atmosphere of mounting dread unsettles the isolated religious community. When an unconventional priest begins investigating the unexplained illness, scientific certainty and religious doctrine collide with an ancient evil: an upyr, the Slavic precursor to the vampire. Following the acclaimed AMIGO (world premiere at Fantastic Fest 2019), director Óscar Martín draws inspiration from the first documented case of vampirism officially recognized by the Catholic Church in Spain, transforming a little-known historical episode into an unsettling exercise in gothic horror. Rather than embracing the familiar iconography of modern vampire cinema, UPIRO returns to the myth's obscure origins, where folklore, history, and collective fear intertwine. Blending the atmosphere of religious horror with the intrigue of a historical mystery, Martín crafts a slow-burning narrative, where silence, ritual, and the oppressive beauty of the rural landscape become as unsettling as the supernatural itself. With stark, somber visuals, tension accumulates with hypnotic precision, revealing a world in which every act of devotion conceals the possibility of corruption, and every attempt to explain the unknown only deepens the mystery. UPIRO explores the enduring power of fear, fanaticism, and inherited trauma, breathing unsettling new life into one of horror's oldest myths while asking whether the darkest monsters are supernatural or born from the stories societies choose to believe in. (SARA LOPO) *Paired with the short FATHER'S LOVE dir.

films.title: Ürei
films.synopsis: When an elderly grandmother is left alone with her young granddaughter, a routine visit gradually gives way to an experience where vulnerability, memory, imagination, and reality begin to blur. Yerkezhan Baizhan, returning with a feature length version of the short that world premiered at FF in 2024, crafts a compact work of horror that is as emotionally resonant as it is unnerving. Avoiding conventional shocks in favor of mounting psychological tension, ÜREI builds its atmosphere through sound and the fragile rhythms of domestic life. The familiar interior of a rural Kazakh home becomes a space where generational bonds coexist with ancient fears, transforming an ordinary act of familial care into an unsettling descent into the unknown. Blurring the boundaries between psychological distress and folklore, Baizhan uses the language of supernatural horror to evoke the emotional realities of grief, loneliness, and the quiet terror of growing old. Through haunting, dark fairy-tale imagery, the film explores the grandmother's increasing isolation and voicelessness alongside the granddaughter's struggle to navigate a world that has suddenly become unfamiliar and threatening. As inherited fears pass between generations, the child is forced to confront mysteries she cannot yet understand, and learn that loss can take monstrous forms. Rooted in the textures of rural Kazakh life yet strikingly universal in its exploration of childhood fear, aging, and mortality, ÜREI suggests that the most terrifying stories are those whispered within families and carried across generations. With remarkable confidence and restraint, Baizhan emerges as a distinctive new voice in contemporary genre cinema, finding profound emotional weight and unexpected tenderness within terror and unease. (SARA LOPO) *Paired with the short THE SUN WON'T SHINE dir.

films.title: Victorian Psycho
films.synopsis: Set in Victorian England, VICTORIAN PSYCHO sees an eccentric governess arrive at a remote gothic manor, where strange happenings stir suspicion that she’s not what she seems. (BLEECKER STREET)

films.title: Visions Of/From South Africa
films.synopsis: In our fourth annual installment of specially curated themed sidebars, Fantastic Fest partners with Durban International Film Festival to present five short films from South Africa. Across genre, time, and place, each explores themes of identity, how we come to be who we are, and the choices we must each make to be true to ourselves. *Please note: films listed in alphabetical order, not in order of appearance in the block. BEING YOU - Dir. Minenhle Luthuli Sheila, an acclaimed screenwriter, has just won an Oscar yet finds herself overwhelmed by the attention. Unable to reconcile lived trauma with present success, she is presented with the opportunity to confront her younger self, desperate to reset the past. B(L)IND THE SACRIFICE - Dir. Nakhane A spiritual leader. A rebellious son, discontent with the status quo. Generational conflict threatens to unravel tradition, religious zealousness, and the stability of the family, questioning faith and devotion to their core. FLEAS - Dir. Jordy Sank Two young Zimbabwean boys live in a South African township, unwelcome as immigrants to say the least. As they wait for their mom to return, the younger brother is in dire need of water. The older brother sets out under dark of night to collect the precious resource. THE HOUSE THAT NEVER SLEEPS - Dir. Sean Mongie An aspiring writer finally gains access to the world of his literary hero, a reclusive author and book binder, who's guarding a variety of secrets within the walls of his family home. A contemplation on the nature and source of the creative spark. SWIM HARD - Dir. Mark Penwill David hires Jess to document his swim team's dream: competing in a new event in the 2028 Olympics. Among other hurdles to overcome in their quest, the coach's event is strictly on shore, no water allowed.

films.title: Welcome to Dolly's House
films.synopsis: The film starts with a marriage proposal in the Paris catacombs. Talk about my dream life. Princess Maria is a rising YouTuber, a ghost-debunking influencer whose life itself is already a performance. She has a vlog with her partner, A-Yue (aka Flawless Florist – yes, yes, you can see where it’s going) entitled Weird Channel. Princess Maria has an endearing personality, but she also is eager to please, and plays a submissive role in their relationship that clashes with her partner’s more stoic, coldly controlling nature. After the catacombs debacle, with the channel losing momentum, Princess Maria receives a video of a disappearing girl. In the background, she notices Madam Dolly, a very famous dollmaker who creates custom, one-of-a-kind dolls. Maria has always owned one of those extremely rare dolls, called Yaya. And in a twist of fate, Madam Dolly is back in Taiwan for the first time in decades to throw a party. Maria has to be there. She and A-Yue engineer access to Dolly’s house because each sees an opportunity in this mythical place very few have entered. Once inside the mansion, however, Maria’s sense of self begins to unravel – helped along by a French-speaking child, much to this French programmer’s delight. Surreal nightmares. Identity crisis. The deeper Maria goes, the more the house forces her to reconsider every relationship she has ever had, and who or what has decided what she could and should become. Taiwan’s first major rotoscoped 2D animated feature is a true visual proposition. The slightly uncanny movements serve the story and themes to a T, carrying the film through a slow descent from mystery into gothic horror.

films.title: What Happened to Doris?
films.synopsis: In 1974, single mother Doris Bither reported being violently assaulted by an unseen force inside her Culver City home. As the attacks escalated, investigators from UCLA documented a series of terrifying events that would become one of the most infamous paranormal cases in American history. Based on the true story that inspired The Entity, WHAT HAPPENED TO DORIS? tells the story through the eyes of the family who lived it. Starring Heather Graham, WHAT HAPPENED TO DORIS? is a harrowing supernatural horror film about an unimaginable haunting—and the devastating cost of refusing to believe its victim.

films.title: Wild Horse Nine
films.synopsis: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways. (SEARCHLIGHT PICTURES)

films.synopsis: Sing and scream your lungs out with Austin’s most entertaining KDJ, Xpider!! It’s Karaoke WITH A TWIST. Come on out and let’s get weird with it.
